events.label: Battle of Mount Gaurus
events.description: battle

story.title: Battle of Mount Gaurus
story.description: First battle of the First Samnite War
paragraphs: The Battle of Mount Gaurus, 343 BC, was the first battle of the First Samnite War and also the first battle fought between the Roman Republic and the Samnites. The battle is described by the Roman historian Livy (59 BC – AD 17) as part of Book Seven of his history of Rome, Ab Urbe Condita Libri, where he narrates how the Roman consul Marcus Valerius Corvus won a hard-fought battle against the Samnites at Mount Gaurus, near Cumae, in Campania. Modern historians however believe that most, if not all, of the detail in Livy's description has been invented by him or his sources.

Bitka pri gori Gaurus (343 pr. n. št.) je bila prva bitka prve samnitske vojne in tudi prva bitka med Rimsko republiko in Samniti. Rimski zgodovinar Livij (59 pr. n. št. – 17 n. št.) jo opisuje v sedmi knjigi svoje zgodovine Rima Ab urbe condita libri (»Knjige od ustanovitve mesta«), kjer pripoveduje, kako je rimski konzul Mark Valerij Korvus v trdi bitki premagal Samnite pri gori Gaurus blizu Kum v Kampaniji. Sodobni zgodovinarji pa menijo, da si je večino podrobnosti Livijevega opisa, če ne vse, izmislil on sam ali njegovi viri.

events.label: Battle of Trifanum
events.description: battle

story.title: Battle of Trifanum
story.description: Battle in 340 BC
paragraphs: The Battle of Trifanum was fought in 340 BC between the Roman Republic and the Latin League. The Roman force was led by Manlius Imperiosus. He pursued the Latins to the north following the Battle of Vesuvius and met them at Trifanum near the mouth of the Liri River. Livy records that the two forces dumped their baggage and fought where they met. He claimed that the Romans were victorious and that their victory was so crushing that afterwards, when the consul entered Latium, the Latins immediately surrendered. As the war continued for another two years it may be that the Latins were surprised at Trifanum and dispersed.

Bitka pri Trifanumu je potekala leta 340 pr. n. št. med Rimsko republiko in latinsko zvezo. Rimsko vojsko je vodil Manlij Imperiosus. Po bitki pri Vezuvu je zasledoval Latince proti severu in se z njimi spopadel pri Trifanumu blizu izliva reke Liri. Livij pripoveduje, da sta obe vojski odvrgli prtljago in se bojevali, kjer sta se srečali. Trdil je, da so Rimljani zmagali in da je bila njihova zmaga tako uničujoča, da so se Latinci takoj vdali, ko je konzul vstopil v Lacij. Ker se je vojna nadaljevala še dve leti, so bili Latinci morda pri Trifanumu presenečeni in razkropljeni.

events.label: Battle of Vesuvius
events.description: 340 BCE battle

story.title: Battle of Vesuvius
story.description: First battle of the Latin War, 340 BC
paragraphs: The Battle of Vesuvius (also known as the Battle of the Veseris) was the first recorded battle of the Latin War. The battle was fought near Mount Vesuvius in 340 BC between the Romans, with their allies the Samnites, against a coalition of several peoples: Latins, Campanians, Volsci, Sidicini, and Aurunci. The surviving sources on the battle, however, focus almost solely on the Romans (led by Titus Manlius Torquatus and Publius Decius Mus) and the Latins.

The battle became famous for two episodes said to have taken place: Manlius Torquatus' execution of his own son after he disobeyed orders and fought an enemy champion in single combat, and the self-sacrifice of Decius Mus, who devoted himself and the enemy army to the gods of the underworld, and then charged into the enemy lines and was slain.

After Decius Mus had fallen, consul Manlius Torquatus led his veteran reserve against Latin lines and killed or captured nearly three fourths of the Latin army. The remaining soldiers of the Latin army fled, but because the Roman loss was so great, they could not pursue their enemies.

Bitka pri Vezuvu (znana tudi kot bitka pri Veserisu) je bila prva zapisana bitka latinske vojne. Potekala je blizu gore Vezuv leta 340 pr. n. št. med Rimljani in njihovimi zavezniki Samniti ter koalicijo več ljudstev: Latincev, Kampancev, Volskov, Sidicinov in Avrunkov. Ohranjeni viri o bitki pa se osredotočajo skoraj izključno na Rimljane (pod vodstvom Tita Manlija Torkvata in Publija Decija Musa) in Latince.

Bitka je zaslovela zaradi dveh epizod, ki naj bi se zgodili: Manlij Torkvat je dal usmrtiti lastnega sina, ker je ta kršil ukaze in se v dvoboju spopadel s sovražnikovim prvakom, Decij Mus pa se je žrtvoval, ko je sebe in sovražno vojsko posvetil podzemnim bogovom, nato pa planil v sovražnikove vrste in padel.

Ko je Decij Mus padel, je konzul Manlij Torkvat s svojo veteransko rezervo napadel latinske vrste in pobil ali ujel skoraj tri četrtine latinske vojske. Preostali vojaki latinske vojske so zbežali, vendar jih zaradi velikih rimskih izgub niso mogli zasledovati.

events.label: Battle of the Caudine Forks
events.description: battle

story.title: Battle of the Caudine Forks
story.description: Battle of the Second Samnite War (321 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Caudine Forks (321 BC) was a decisive event of the Second Samnite War. Its designation as a battle is a mere historical formality: there was no fighting and there were no casualties. The Romans were trapped in an enclosed valley by the Samnites before they knew what was happening and nothing remained but to negotiate an unfavorable surrender. The action was entirely political, with the magistrates on both sides trying to obtain the best terms for their side without disrespecting common beliefs concerning the rules of war and the conduct of peace. In the end the Samnites decided it would be better for future relations to let the Romans go, while the Romans were impeded in the prosecution of their campaign against the Samnites by considerations of religion and honor.

Bitka pri Kavdinskih soteskah (321 pr. n. št.) je bila odločilen dogodek druge samnitske vojne. Da je to bitka, je zgolj zgodovinska formalnost: bojev ni bilo in izgub tudi ne. Samniti so Rimljane ujeli v zaprti dolini, še preden so ti ugotovili, kaj se dogaja, in nič drugega jim ni preostalo, kot da se pogajajo o neugodni vdaji. Dogajanje je bilo povsem politično: magistrati na obeh straneh so skušali doseči najboljše pogoje za svojo stran, ne da bi žalili splošno sprejeta prepričanja o pravilih vojne in ravnanju v miru. Nazadnje so se Samniti odločili, da bo za prihodnje odnose bolje, če Rimljane izpustijo, Rimljane pa so pri nadaljevanju pohoda proti Samnitom ovirali verski razlogi in čast.

events.label: Battle of Lautulae
events.description: battle

story.title: Battle of Lautulae
story.description: Battle in 315 BC during the Second Samnite War
paragraphs: The Battle of Lautulae was fought in 315 BC during the Second Samnite War, opposing the Roman Republic (led by dictator Quintus Fabius Maximus Rullianus) and the Samnites, who defeated the Romans.

Bitka pri Lautulae je potekala leta 315 pr. n. št. v drugi samnitski vojni; v njej sta se spopadla Rimska republika (pod vodstvom diktatorja Kvinta Fabija Maksima Rulijana) in Samniti, ki so Rimljane porazili.

events.label: Battle of Lake Vadimo
events.description: 310 BCE battle

story.title: Battle of Lake Vadimo (310 BC)
story.description: Battle in 310 BC
paragraphs: The first Battle of Lake Vadimo was fought in 310 BC between Rome and the Etruscans, and ended up being the largest battle between these nations. The Romans were victorious, gaining land and influence in the region. The Etruscans sustained heavy losses in the battle and would never again reclaim their previous glory.

Prva bitka pri jezeru Vadimo je potekala leta 310 pr. n. št. med Rimom in Etruščani in je postala največja bitka med tema narodoma. Rimljani so zmagali in pridobili zemljo in vpliv v regiji. Etruščani so v bitki utrpeli hude izgube in svoje nekdanje slave nikoli več niso dosegli.

events.label: Battle of Bovianum
events.description: 304 BCE battle

story.title: Battle of Bovianum
story.description: 305 BC battle between the Romans and the Samnites
paragraphs: The Battle of Bovianum was fought in 305 BC between the Romans and the Samnites.
Bitka pri Bovianumu je potekala leta 305 pr. n. št. med Rimljani in Samniti.

events.label: Battle of Sentinum
events.description: 295 BCE battle of the Third Samnite War

story.title: Battle of Sentinum
story.description: Battle of the Third Samnite War (295 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Sentinum was the decisive battle of the Third Samnite War, fought in 295 BC near Sentinum (next to the modern town of Sassoferrato, in the Marches region of Italy), in which the Romans overcame a formidable coalition of Samnites, Etruscans, Umbrians, and Senone Gauls. The Romans won a decisive victory that broke up the tribal coalition (the Etruscans, Umbrians, and Senones pulled out of the war) and paved the way for the Romans' complete victory over the Samnites. The Romans involved in the battle of Sentinum were commanded by consuls Publius Decius Mus and Quintus Fabius Maximus Rullianus.

Bitka pri Sentinumu je bila odločilna bitka tretje samnitske vojne, ki je potekala leta 295 pr. n. št. blizu Sentinuma (ob današnjem mestu Sassoferrato v italijanski deželi Marke). V njej so Rimljani premagali mogočno koalicijo Samnitov, Etruščanov, Umbrov in galskih Senonov. Odločilna rimska zmaga je koalicijo plemen razbila (Etruščani, Umbri in Senoni so se umaknili iz vojne) in utrla pot popolni rimski zmagi nad Samniti. Rimskim silam v bitki sta poveljevala konzula Publij Decij Mus in Kvint Fabij Maksim Rulijan.

events.label: Battle of Arretium
events.description: battle during the Roman–Gallic wars (c.284 BC)

story.title: Battle of Arretium
story.description: Battle during the Roman–Gallic wars (c.284 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Arretium, which was probably fought in 284 BC, is a poorly documented event in the history of the Roman Republic because it occurred in a period for which some of the books of the History of Rome by Livy, the most thorough ancient historian for early Rome, have been lost. The battle is only explicitly referred to in a text by Polybius, the ancient Greek historian, which does not give much detail and puts it in the context of other events. A text by Appian talks about these events, but does not make any explicit reference to the Battle of Arretium. It was fought between the Romans and the Gauls of northern Italy, who may have been from the Senone tribe.

According to Polybius, unspecified Gauls besieged the city of Arretium (Arezzo, in northeastern Tuscany) and defeated a Roman force which had come to the aid of the city. Their commander, the praetor Lucius Caecilius Metellus Denter, died in the battle. This would place the battle in 283 BC because Denter was a consul in 284 BC.

Bitka pri Arretiumu, ki je verjetno potekala leta 284 pr. n. št., je slabo dokumentiran dogodek iz zgodovine Rimske republike, ker se je zgodila v obdobju, za katero so nekatere knjige Livijeve Rimske zgodovine, najpodrobnejšega antičnega zgodovinarja zgodnjega Rima, izgubljene. Bitka je izrecno omenjena le v besedilu Polibija, antičnega grškega zgodovinarja, ki ne navaja veliko podrobnosti in jo postavlja v okvir drugih dogodkov. O teh dogodkih govori tudi besedilo Apijana, a bitke pri Arretiumu izrecno ne omenja. Bitka je bila med Rimljani in Galci iz severne Italije, ki so bili morda iz plemena Senonov.

Po Polibiju so neimenovani Galci oblegali mesto Arretium (Arezzo na severovzhodu Toskane) in porazili rimsko vojsko, ki je mestu prišla na pomoč. Njihov poveljnik, pretor Lucij Cecilij Metel Denter, je v bitki padel. Zato bi bitka spadala v leto 283 pr. n. št., ker je bil Denter konzul leta 284 pr. n. št.

events.label: Battle of Lake Vadimo
events.description: Roman Republic victory over a joint Etruscan -Gaulish army

story.title: Battle of Lake Vadimon (283 BC)
story.description: Battle in 283 BC
paragraphs: The second Battle of Lake Vadimo was fought in 283 BC between Rome and the combined forces of the Etruscans and the Gallic tribes of the Boii and the Senones. The Roman army was led by consul Publius Cornelius Dolabella. The result of the battle was a Roman victory.

Druga bitka pri jezeru Vadimo je potekala leta 283 pr. n. št. med Rimom in združenimi silami Etruščanov ter galskih plemen Bojev in Senonov. Rimsko vojsko je vodil konzul Publij Kornelij Dolabela. Bitka se je končala z rimsko zmago.

events.label: Battle of Heraclea
events.description: battle

story.title: Battle of Heraclea
story.description: Battle in 280 BC between the Romans and Pyrrhus of Epirus
paragraphs: The Battle of Heraclea took place in 280 BC between the Romans under the command of consul Publius Valerius Laevinus, and the combined forces of Greeks from Epirus, Tarentum, Thurii, Metapontum, and Heraclea under the command of Pyrrhus, king of Epirus. Although the battle was a victory for the Greeks, they incurred severe losses.

Bitka pri Herakleji je potekala leta 280 pr. n. št. med Rimljani pod poveljstvom konzula Publija Valerija Levina in združenimi silami Grkov iz Epira, Tarenta, Turijev, Metaponta in Herakleje pod poveljstvom Pira, epirskega kralja. Čeprav je bila bitka grška zmaga, so Grki utrpeli hude izgube.

events.label: Battle of Asculum
events.description: 279 BCE battle of the Pyrrhic War,battle

story.title: Battle of Asculum
story.description: 279 BC battle of the Pyrrhic War
paragraphs: The Battle of Asculum was a battle that took place near Asculum (modern Ascoli Satriano) in 279 BC, and was thought to have lasted either one or two days, between the Roman Republic under the command of the consuls Publius Decius Mus (who by some accounts died before the battle) and Publius Sulpicius Saverrio, and the forces of King Pyrrhus of Epirus. The battle took place during the Pyrrhic War, after the Battle of Heraclea of 280 BC, which was the first battle of the war. There currently exist accounts of this battle only by three ancient historians: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Plutarch, and Cassius Dio, although these historians in turn reference other historians whose work is now lost. Asculum was in Lucanian territory, in southern Italy.

The Battle of Asculum was the original "Pyrrhic victory". Two main accounts of the battle survive. Plutarch describes a two-day battle where Pyrrhus attacked the Romans on the first day over rough terrain before on the second day Pyrrhus secured flat terrain which allowed his elephants, infantry and cavalry to defeat the Romans. Dionysius of Halicarnassus, followed by Dio and Zonaras, instead presents a single-day battle in which Roman forces break through the Epirote centre, producing an inconclusive engagement that ended in the night. Plutarch's narrative however is the more reliable. A third variant tradition, rather than marking a Epirote victory or indecision, instead reports that the Romans won; the historian Patrick Kent dismisses these claims as products of patriotic Roman historiography, attributing them to the poet Ennius and later Roman historians' biases. Jeff Champion suggests that it was a narrow tactical victory to Pyrrhus.

Bitka pri Askulu je bila bitka, ki je potekala blizu Askula (današnji Ascoli Satriano) leta 279 pr. n. št. in je po mnenju nekaterih trajala en dan, po mnenju drugih dva. Na eni strani je bila Rimska republika pod poveljstvom konzulov Publija Decija Musa (ki je po nekaterih virih umrl že pred bitko) in Publija Sulpicija Saverriona, na drugi pa vojska epirskega kralja Pira. Bitka je potekala v Pirovi vojni, po bitki pri Heraklei leta 280 pr. n. št., prvi bitki te vojne. Obstajajo samo poročila treh antičnih zgodovinarjev, Dionizija Halikarnaškega, Plutarha in Kasija Diona, čeprav ti sami navajajo druge zgodovinarje, katerih dela so danes izgubljena. Askul je bil na ozemlju Lukancev v južni Italiji.

events.label: Battle of Beneventum
events.description: battle fought in 275 BCE

story.title: Battle of Beneventum (275 BC)
story.description: 275 BC Battle of the Pyrrhic war
paragraphs: The Battle of Beneventum (275 BC) was the last battle of the Pyrrhic War. It was fought near Beneventum, in southern Italy, between the forces of Pyrrhus, king of Epirus in Greece, and the Romans, led by consul Manius Curius Dentatus. The result was a strategic Roman victory and Pyrrhus was forced to return to Tarentum, and later to Epirus.

Bitka pri Beneventu (275 pr. n. št.) je bila zadnja bitka Pirove vojne. Potekala je blizu Beneventuma v južni Italiji med silami Pira, kralja Epira v Grčiji, in Rimljani pod poveljstvom konzula Manija Kurija Dentata. Izid je bil strateška rimska zmaga, Pir pa se je moral vrniti v Tarent in pozneje v Epir.

events.label: Battle of Messana
events.description: first military conflict between the Roman Republic and Carthage, marking the start of the First Punic War

story.title: Battle of Messana
story.description: Battle between Rome and Carthage
paragraphs: The Battle of Messana in 264 BC was the first military clash between the Roman Republic and Carthage. It marked the start of the First Punic War. In that period, and after the recent successes in southern Italy, Sicily became of increasing strategic importance to Rome.

Bitka pri Mesini leta 264 pr. n. št. je bila prvi vojaški spopad med Rimsko republiko in Kartagino. Z njo se je začela prva punska vojna. Po nedavnih uspehih v južni Italiji je Sicilija tedaj za Rim postajala strateško vse pomembnejša.

events.label: Battle of Agrigentum
events.description: first pitched battle of the First Punic War and the first large-scale military confrontation between Carthage and the Roman Republic

story.title: Battle of Agrigentum
story.description: 262 BC naval battle between Carthage and Rome
paragraphs: The Battle of Agrigentum (Sicily, 262 BC) was the first pitched battle of the First Punic War and the first large-scale military confrontation between Carthage and the Roman Republic. The battle was fought after a long siege which started in 262 BC and resulted both in a Roman victory and the beginning of Roman control of Sicily.

Bitka pri Agrigentu (Sicilija, 262 pr. n. št.) je bila prva odprta bitka prve punske vojne in prvi velik vojaški spopad med Kartagino in Rimsko republiko. Bitka je sledila dolgemu obleganju, ki se je začelo leta 262 pr. n. št., in se je končala z rimsko zmago ter začetkom rimskega nadzora nad Sicilijo.

events.label: Battle of Mylae
events.description: first real naval battle between Carthage and the Roman Republic in the First Punic War

story.title: Battle of Mylae
story.description: Naval battle in 260 BC
paragraphs: The Battle of Mylae took place in 260 BC during the First Punic War and was the first real naval battle between Carthage and the Roman Republic. This battle was key in the Roman victory of Mylae (present-day Milazzo) as well as Sicily itself. It also marked Rome's first naval triumph and also the first use of the corvus in battle.

Bitka pri Milah je potekala leta 260 pr. n. št. v prvi punski vojni in je bila prva prava pomorska bitka med Kartagino in Rimsko republiko. Bila je ključna za rimsko zmago pri Milah (današnji Milazzo) in za Sicilijo samo. Pomenila je tudi prvi rimski pomorski triumf in prvo uporabo korvusa v bitki.

events.label: Battle of the Lipari Islands
events.description: first encounter between the fleets of Carthage and the Roman Republic during the First Punic War

events.label: Battle of Sulci
events.description: naval battle fought in 258 BCE between the Roman and Carthaginian navies on the coast near the town of Sulci, Sardinia

story.title: Battle of Sulci
story.description: 258 BC defeat for the Carthaginian navy
paragraphs: The Battle of Sulci was a naval battle fought in 258 BC between the Roman and Carthaginian navies on the coast near the town of Sulci, Sardinia. It was a Roman victory, obtained by consul Gaius Sulpicius Paterculus. The Carthaginian fleet was largely sunk, and the rest of the ships were abandoned on land. The Carthaginian commander Hannibal Gisco was crucified or stoned to death by his mutinying army.

The Romans were subsequently defeated by a certain Hanno in Sardinia, and the Roman attempt to capture the island failed. The loss of ships prevented the Carthaginians from mounting major operations from Sardinia against the Romans.

Bitka pri Sulciju je bila pomorska bitka, ki je potekala leta 258 pr. n. št. med rimskim in kartažanskim ladjevjem ob obali blizu mesta Sulci na Sardiniji. Bila je rimska zmaga, ki jo je dosegel konzul Gaj Sulpicij Paterkul. Kartažansko ladjevje so večinoma potopili, preostale ladje pa so pustili na kopnem. Kartažanskega poveljnika Hanibala Giskona je njegova vojska, ki se je uprla, razpela na križ ali ubila s kamenjanjem.
Rimljane je pozneje na Sardiniji premagal nek Hanon in rimski poskus zavzetja otoka je spodletel. Zaradi izgube ladij Kartažani s Sardinije niso mogli začeti večjih operacij proti Rimljanom.

events.label: Battle of Tyndaris
events.description: naval battle of the First Punic War that took place off Tyndaris (modern Tindari) in 257 BCE

story.title: Battle of Tyndaris
story.description: Naval battle of the First Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of Tyndaris was a naval battle of the First Punic War that took place off Tyndaris (modern Tindari) in 257 BC. Tyndaris was a Sicilian town founded as a Greek colony in 396 BC located on the high ground overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea in the Gulf of Patti. Hiero II, the tyrant of Syracuse, allowed Tyndaris to become a base for the Carthaginians. The battle took place in the waters between Tyndaris and the Aeolian Islands, with Gaius Atilius Regulus in command of the Roman fleet. Subsequently, the town fell to Rome.

Bitka pri Tindaridi je bila pomorska bitka prve punske vojne, ki je potekala leta 257 pr. n. št. pred Tindarido (današnji Tindari). Tindarida je bilo sicilsko mesto, ustanovljeno leta 396 pr. n. št. kot grška kolonija na visokem svetu nad Tirenskim morjem v zalivu Patti. Hieron II., sirakuški tiran, je dovolil, da je Tindarida postala oporišče Kartažanov. Bitka je potekala v vodah med Tindarido in Eolskimi otoki, rimskemu ladjevju pa je poveljeval Gaj Atilij Regul. Mesto je nato padlo v rimske roke.

events.label: Battle of Cape Ecnomus
events.description: naval battle of the First Punic War fought off Cape Ecnomus (modern day Poggio di Sant'Angelo in Licata, Sicily) and one of the largest naval battles of the ancient world

story.title: Battle of Cape Ecnomus
story.description: Naval battle of the First Punic War; possibly the largest in history
paragraphs: The Battle of Cape Ecnomus or Eknomos (Ancient Greek: Ἔκνομος) was a naval battle, fought off southern Sicily, in 256 BC, between the fleets of Carthage and the Roman Republic, during the First Punic War (264–241 BC). The Carthaginian fleet was commanded by Hanno and Hamilcar; the Roman fleet jointly by the consuls for the year, Marcus Atilius Regulus and Lucius Manlius Vulso Longus. It resulted in a clear victory for the Romans.

The Roman fleet of 330 warships plus an unknown number of transports had sailed from Ostia, the port of Rome, and had embarked approximately 26,000 picked legionaries shortly before the battle. They planned to cross to Africa and invade the Carthaginian homeland, in Tunisia. The Carthaginians were aware of the Romans' intentions and mustered all available warships, 350, off the south coast of Sicily to intercept them. With a combined total of about 680 warships carrying up to 290,000 crew and marines, the battle was arguably the single largest battle of ancient history, and was possibly the largest naval battle in history by the number of combatants involved.

When the fleets met, the Carthaginians took the initiative and the battle devolved into three separate conflicts, where the Carthaginians hoped that their superior ship-handling skills would win the day. After a prolonged and confusing day of fighting, the Carthaginians were decisively defeated, losing 30 ships sunk and 64 captured to Roman losses of 24 ships sunk.

Bitka pri rtu Ecnomus ali Eknomos (starogrško: Ἔκνομος) je bila pomorska bitka, ki je potekala ob južni Siciliji leta 256 pr. n. št. med ladjevjema Kartagine in Rimske republike v prvi punski vojni (264–241 pr. n. št.). Kartažanskemu ladjevju sta poveljevala Hanon in Hamilkar, rimskemu pa skupaj tedanja konzula Mark Atilij Regul in Lucij Manlij Vulson Longus. Končala se je z jasno rimsko zmago.

Rimsko ladjevje s 330 vojaškimi ladjami in neznanim številom transportnih ladij je izplulo iz Ostije, rimskega pristanišča, in tik pred bitko vkrcalo približno 26.000 izbranih legionarjev. Nameravali so prečkati morje do Afrike in vdreti v kartažansko domovino, v današnji Tuniziji. Kartažani so poznali rimske namere in zbrali vse razpoložljive vojaške ladje, 350, ob južni obali Sicilije, da bi jih prestregli. Z okoli 680 vojaškimi ladjami in do 290.000 možmi posadk in mornariških pehotincev je bila bitka morda največja posamična bitka antične zgodovine, po številu udeležencev pa verjetno tudi največja pomorska bitka v zgodovini.

events.label: Battle of Adys
events.description: battle of the First Punic War in which Rome defeated Carthage

story.title: Battle of Adys
story.description: 256 BC battle of the First Punic War
paragraphs: The battle of Adys (or Adis) took place in late 256 BC during the First Punic War between a Carthaginian army jointly commanded by Bostar, Hamilcar and Hasdrubal and a Roman army led by Marcus Atilius Regulus. Earlier in the year, the new Roman navy had established naval superiority and used this advantage to invade the Carthaginian homeland, which roughly aligned with modern Tunisia in North Africa. After landing on the Cape Bon Peninsula and conducting a successful campaign, the fleet returned to Sicily, leaving Regulus with 15,500 men to hold the lodgement in Africa over the winter.

Instead of holding his position, Regulus advanced towards the Carthaginian capital, Carthage. The Carthaginian army established itself on a rocky hill near Adys (modern Uthina) where Regulus was besieging the town. Regulus had his forces execute a night march to launch twin dawn assaults on the Carthaginians' fortified hilltop camp. One part of this force was repulsed and pursued down the hill. The other part then charged the pursuing Carthaginians in the rear and routed them in turn. At this the Carthaginians remaining in the camp panicked and fled.

The Romans advanced to and captured Tunis, only 16 kilometres (10 mi) from Carthage. Despairing, the Carthaginians sued for peace. The terms offered by Regulus were so harsh that Carthage resolved to fight on. A few months later, at the battle of the Bagradas River (battle of Tunis), Regulus was defeated and his army all but wiped out. The war continued for a further 14 years.

Bitka pri Adisu je potekala konec leta 256 pr. n. št. med prvo punsko vojno med kartažansko vojsko, ki so ji skupaj poveljevali Bostar, Hamilkar in Hasdrubal, ter rimsko vojsko pod vodstvom Marka Atilija Regula. Prej tistega leta si je nova rimska vojna mornarica zagotovila premoč na morju in jo izkoristila za vdor v kartažansko domovino, ki je približno ustrezala današnji Tuniziji v severni Afriki. Ko se je ladjevje izkrcalo na polotoku Cap Bon in izvedlo uspešen pohod, se je vrnilo na Sicilijo, Regulu pa je pustilo 15.500 mož, da bi čez zimo obdržal mostišče v Afriki.

events.label: Battle of Bagradas
events.wiki: Battle of the Bagradas River (255 BC)
events.description: battle of the First Punic War with a Carthaginian victory
events.sl: Bitka pri Bagradi (255 pr. n. št.)

story.title: Battle of the Bagradas River (255 BC)
story.description: Battle of the First Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of the Bagradas River (the ancient name of the Medjerda), also known as the Battle of Tunis, was a victory by a Carthaginian army led by Xanthippus over a Roman army led by Marcus Atilius Regulus in the spring of 255 BC, nine years into the First Punic War. The previous year, the newly constructed Roman navy established naval superiority over Carthage. The Romans used this advantage to invade Carthage's homeland, which roughly aligned with modern-day Tunisia in North Africa. After landing on the Cape Bon Peninsula and conducting a successful campaign, the fleet returned to Sicily, leaving Regulus with 15,500 men to hold the lodgement in Africa over the winter.

Instead of holding his position, Regulus advanced towards the city of Carthage and defeated the Carthaginian army at the Battle of Adys. The Romans followed up and captured Tunis, only 16 kilometres (10 mi) from Carthage. Despairing, the Carthaginians sued for peace, but Regulus's proposed terms were so harsh the Carthaginians decided to fight on. They gave charge of the training of their army, and eventually operational control, to the Spartan mercenary general Xanthippus.

In the spring of 255 BC, Xanthippus led an army strong in cavalry and elephants against the Romans' infantry-based force. The Romans had no effective answer to the elephants. Their outnumbered cavalry were chased from the field and the Carthaginian cavalry then surrounded most of the Romans and wiped them out; 500 survived and were captured, including Regulus. A force of 2,000 Romans avoided being surrounded and retreated to Aspis. The war continued for another 14 years, mostly on Sicily or in nearby waters, before ending with a Roman victory; the terms offered to Carthage were more generous than those proposed by Regulus.

Bitka pri reki Bagradi (antično ime Medžerde), znana tudi kot bitka pri Tunisu, je bila zmaga kartažanske vojske pod vodstvom Ksantipa nad rimsko vojsko pod vodstvom Marka Atilija Regula spomladi leta 255 pr. n. št., v devetem letu prve punske vojne. Leto prej si je novo zgrajena rimska vojna mornarica zagotovila premoč na morju nad Kartagino. Rimljani so to prednost izkoristili za vdor v kartažansko domovino, ki je približno ustrezala današnji Tuniziji v severni Afriki. Ko se je ladjevje izkrcalo na polotoku Cap Bon in izvedlo uspešen pohod, se je vrnilo na Sicilijo, Regulu pa je pustilo 15.500 mož, da bi čez zimo obdržal mostišče v Afriki.

events.label: Battle of Panormus
events.description: Roman victory leading to Panormus (modern-day Palermo) being under Roman control for the remainder of the First Punic War

story.title: Battle of Panormus
story.description: Battle of the First Punic War, 250 BCE
paragraphs: The Battle of Panormus was fought in Sicily in 250 BC during the First Punic War between a Roman army led by Lucius Caecilius Metellus and a Carthaginian force led by Hasdrubal, son of Hanno. The Roman force of two Roman and two allied legions defending the city of Panormus defeated the much larger Carthaginian army of 30,000 men and between 60 and 142 war elephants.

The war had commenced in 264 BC with Carthage in control of much of Sicily, where most of the fighting took place. In 256–255 BC the Romans attempted to strike at the city of Carthage in North Africa, but suffered a heavy defeat by a Carthaginian army strong in cavalry and elephants. When the focus of the war returned to Sicily, the Romans captured the large and important city of Panormus in 254 BC. Thereafter they avoided battle for fear of the war elephants which the Carthaginians had shipped to Sicily. In late summer 250 BC Hasdrubal led out his army to devastate the crops of the cities of Rome's allies. The Romans withdrew to Panormus and Hasdrubal pressed on to the city walls.

Once he arrived in Panormus, Metellus turned to fight, countering the elephants with a hail of javelins from earthworks dug near the walls. Under this missile fire the elephants panicked and fled through the Carthaginian infantry. The Roman heavy infantry then charged the Carthaginian left flank, which broke, along with the rest of the Carthaginians. The elephants were captured and later slaughtered in the Circus Maximus. This was the last significant land battle of the war, which ended nine years later in a Roman victory.

Bitka pri Panormu je potekala na Siciliji leta 250 pr. n. št. v prvi punski vojni med rimsko vojsko pod poveljstvom Lucija Cecilija Metela in kartažanskimi silami pod poveljstvom Hasdrubala, Hanonovega sina. Rimske sile, dve rimski in dve zavezniški legiji, ki so branile mesto Panorm, so premagale veliko močnejšo kartažansko vojsko s 30.000 možmi in od 60 do 142 bojnimi slonovi.

Vojna se je začela leta 264 pr. n. št., ko je Kartagina nadzorovala velik del Sicilije, kjer je potekala večina bojev. Leta 256–255 pr. n. št. so Rimljani skušali udariti po mestu Kartagina v Severni Afriki, a jih je kartažanska vojska, močna v konjenici in slonih, hudo porazila. Ko se je težišče vojne vrnilo na Sicilijo, so Rimljani leta 254 pr. n. št. zavzeli veliko in pomembno mesto Panorm. Nato so se zaradi strahu pred bojnimi slonovi, ki so jih Kartažani pripeljali na Sicilijo, izogibali bitki. Ob koncu poletja 250 pr. n. št. je Hasdrubal popeljal vojsko, da bi opustošil pridelke v mestih rimskih zaveznikov. Rimljani so se umaknili v Panorm, Hasdrubal pa je prodrl do mestnega obzidja.

events.label: Siege of Lilybaeum
events.description: battle of the First Punic War resulting in a Roman retreat

story.title: Siege of Lilybaeum (250–241 BC)
story.description: Roman siege of a Carthaginian city during the First Punic War
paragraphs: The siege of Lilybaeum lasted for nine years, from 250 to 241 BC, as the Roman army laid siege to the Carthaginian-held Sicilian city of Lilybaeum (modern Marsala) during the First Punic War. Rome and Carthage had been at war since 264 BC, fighting mostly on the island of Sicily or in the waters around it, and the Romans were slowly pushing the Carthaginians back. By 250 BC, the Carthaginians held only the cities of Lilybaeum and Drepana; these were well-fortified and situated on the west coast, where they could be supplied and reinforced by sea without the Romans being able to use their superior army to interfere.

In mid-250 BC the Romans besieged Lilybaeum with more than 100,000 men but an attempt to storm Lilybaeum failed and the siege became a stalemate. The Romans then attempted to destroy the Carthaginian fleet but the Roman fleet was destroyed in the naval Battles of Drepana and Phintias; the Carthaginians continued to supply the city from the sea. Nine years later, in 242 BC, the Romans built a new fleet and cut off Carthaginian shipments. The Carthaginians reconstituted their fleet and dispatched it to Sicily loaded with supplies. The Romans met it not far from Lilybaeum and at the Battle of the Aegates in 241 BC the Romans defeated the Carthaginian fleet. The Carthaginians sued for peace and the war ended after 23 years with a Roman victory. The Carthaginians still held Lilybaeum but by the terms of the Treaty of Lutatius, Carthage had to withdraw its forces from Sicily and evacuated the city the same year.

Obleganje Lilibeja je trajalo devet let, od 250 do 241 pr. n. št., ko je rimska vojska v prvi punski vojni oblegala kartažansko sicilsko mesto Lilibej (današnja Marsala). Rim in Kartagina sta bila v vojni od leta 264 pr. n. št., bojevala sta se večinoma na Siciliji ali v okoliških vodah, Rimljani pa so Kartažane počasi potiskali nazaj. Do leta 250 pr. n. št. so Kartažani držali le še mesti Lilibej in Drepana; bili sta dobro utrjeni in ležali na zahodni obali, kjer ju je bilo mogoče oskrbovati in okrepiti po morju, ne da bi lahko Rimljani s svojo močnejšo kopensko vojsko posegli vmes.

events.label: Battle of Drepana
events.description: naval battle of the First Punic War near modern Trapani, western Sicily, with the Carthaginian fleet emerging victorious

story.title: Battle of Drepana
story.description: 249 BC Carthaginian naval victory in the First Punic War
paragraphs: The naval Battle of Drepana (or Drepanum) took place in 249 BC during the First Punic War near Drepana (modern Trapani) in western Sicily, between a Carthaginian fleet under Adherbal and a Roman fleet commanded by Publius Claudius Pulcher.

Pulcher was blockading the Carthaginian stronghold of Lilybaeum (modern Marsala) when he decided to attack their fleet, which was in the harbour of the nearby city of Drepana. The Roman fleet sailed by night to carry out a surprise attack but became scattered in the dark. Adherbal was able to lead his fleet out to sea before it was trapped in harbour; having gained sea room in which to manoeuvre he then counter-attacked. The Romans were pinned against the shore, and after a day of fighting were heavily defeated by the more manoeuvrable Carthaginian ships with their better-trained crews. It was Carthage's greatest naval victory of the war; they turned to the maritime offensive after Drepana and all but swept the Romans from the sea. It was seven years before Rome again attempted to field a substantial fleet, while Carthage put most of its ships into reserve to save money and free up manpower.

Pomorska bitka pri Drepani (ali Drepanumu) je potekala leta 249 pr. n. št. v prvi punski vojni blizu Drepane (današnji Trapani) v zahodni Siciliji med kartažanskim ladjevjem pod Adherbalom in rimskim ladjevjem pod poveljstvom Publija Klavdija Pulhra.

events.label: Battle of the Aegates Islands
events.description: final naval battle between Carthage and the Roman Republic in the First Punic War, resulting in a decisive Roman victory

story.title: Battle of the Aegates
story.description: Carthage-Rome naval battle, 241 BCE
paragraphs: The Battle of the Aegates was a naval battle fought on 10 March 241 BC between the fleets of Carthage and Rome during the First Punic War. It took place among the Aegates Islands, off the western coast of the island of Sicily. The Carthaginians were commanded by Hanno, and the Romans were under the overall authority of Gaius Lutatius Catulus, but Quintus Valerius Falto commanded during the battle. It was the final and deciding battle of the 23-year-long First Punic War.

The Roman army had been blockading the Carthaginians in their last strongholds on the west coast of Sicily for several years. Almost bankrupt, the Romans borrowed money to build a naval fleet, which they used to extend the blockade to the sea. The Carthaginians assembled a larger fleet which they intended to use to run supplies into Sicily. It would then embark much of the Carthaginian army stationed there as marines. It was intercepted by the Roman fleet and in a hard-fought battle, the better-trained Romans defeated the undermanned and ill-trained Carthaginian fleet, which was further handicapped by being laden with supplies and having not yet embarked its full complement of marines.

As a direct result, Carthage sued for peace and agreed to the Treaty of Lutatius, by which Carthage surrendered Sicily to Rome and paid substantial reparations. Henceforth Rome was the leading military power in the western Mediterranean, and increasingly the Mediterranean region as a whole.

Bitka pri Egatskih otokih je bila pomorska bitka, ki je potekala 10. marca 241 pr. n. št. med ladjevjema Kartagine in Rima v prvi punski vojni. Bojevali so se med Egatskimi otoki ob zahodni obali Sicilije. Kartažanom je poveljeval Hanon, Rimljane pa je vrhovno vodil Gaj Lutacij Katul, med samo bitko pa jim je poveljeval Kvint Valerij Falton. Bila je zadnja in odločilna bitka 23 let trajajoče prve punske vojne.

events.label: Battle of Telamon
events.description: battle between the Romans and the Celts (225 BC)

story.title: Battle of Telamon
story.description: Battle between the Romans and the Celts (225 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Telamon was fought between the Roman Republic and an alliance of Celtic tribes in 225 BC. The Romans, led by the consuls Gaius Atilius Regulus and Lucius Aemilius Papus, defeated the Celts led by the Gaesatae kings Concolitanus and Aneroëstes. This removed the Celtic threat from Rome and allowed the Romans to extend their influence over northern Italy.

Bitka pri Telamonu je potekala leta 225 pr. n. št. med Rimsko republiko in zavezništvom keltskih plemen. Rimljani pod vodstvom konzulov Gaja Atilija Regula in Lucija Emilija Papusa so premagali Kelte pod vodstvom gezatskih kraljev Koncolitana in Aneroësta. Tako je bila keltska grožnja Rimu odpravljena, Rimljani pa so lahko razširili svoj vpliv nad severno Italijo.

events.label: Battle of Clastidium
events.description: battle during the Roman-Gaulish wars (222 BC)

story.title: Battle of Clastidium
story.description: Battle during the Roman-Gallic wars (222 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Clastidium was fought in 222 BC between a Roman army led by the consul Marcus Claudius Marcellus and a Celtic force of the transalpine Gaesatae, called by the cisalpine Insubres. The Gaesatae were led by Viridomarus (Florus) or Britomartus (Plutarch), as the name varies in translation. The Romans won the battle, and in the process, Marcellus earned the spolia opima, one of the highest honors in ancient Rome, by killing the king in single combat. It was also notable as one of the few battles won by the Roman cavalry without any aid by the legions.

events.label: Siege of Saguntum
events.description: 219 BCE battle between the Carthaginians and the Saguntines in the Roman-allied town of Saguntum (in modern-day Sagunto, Spain), triggering the Second Punic War

story.title: Siege of Saguntum
story.description: 219 BC Carthaginian victory starting the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The siege of Saguntum took place in 219 BC between the Carthaginians and the Saguntines at the town of Saguntum, near the modern town of Sagunto in the province of Valencia, Spain. The battle is mainly remembered today because it triggered one of the most important wars of antiquity, the Second Punic War.

Obleganje Sagunta je potekalo leta 219 pr. n. št. med Kartažani in Saguntinci pri mestu Saguntum blizu današnjega mesta Sagunto v provinci Valencia v Španiji. Bitke se danes spominjamo predvsem zato, ker je sprožila eno najpomembnejših vojn antike, drugo punsko vojno.

events.label: Battle of Cissa
events.description: 218 BCE battle of the Second Punic War, the first battle that the Romans fought in Iberia

story.title: Battle of Cissa
story.description: 218 BC battle in Spain, part of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of Cissa was part of the Second Punic War. It was fought in the fall of 218 BC, near the town of Tarraco in north-eastern Iberia. A Roman army under Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Calvus defeated an outnumbered Carthaginian army under Hanno, thus gaining control of the territory north of the Ebro River that Hannibal had just subdued a few months prior in the summer of 218 BC. This was the first battle that the Romans had ever fought in Iberia.

It allowed the Romans to establish a secure base among friendly Iberian tribes, and due to the eventual success of the Scipio brothers in Spain, Hannibal looked for but never received reinforcements from Spain during the war.

Bitka pri Cissi je bila del druge punske vojne. Potekala je jeseni 218 pr. n. št. blizu mesta Tarraco na severovzhodu Iberskega polotoka. Rimska vojska pod Gnejem Kornelijem Scipionom Kalvom je premagala številčno šibkejšo kartažansko vojsko pod Hanonom in tako prevzela nadzor nad ozemljem severno od reke Ebro, ki ga je Hanibal podjarmil le nekaj mesecev prej, poleti 218 pr. n. št. To je bila prva bitka, v kateri so se Rimljani kdaj bojevali na Iberskem polotoku.

Rimljanom je omogočila, da so si med prijateljskimi iberskimi plemeni ustvarili varno oporišče, in zaradi poznejšega uspeha bratov Scipionov v Hispaniji Hanibal med vojno ni nikoli dobil okrepitev iz Hispanije, čeprav jih je iskal.

events.label: Battle of Lilybaeum
events.description: first naval clash between the navies of Carthage and Rome during the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Lilybaeum
story.description: First naval clash between the navies of Carthage and Rome during the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of Lilybaeum was the first clash between the navies of Carthage and Rome in 218 BC during the Second Punic War. The Carthaginians had sent 35 quinqueremes to raid Sicily, starting with Lilybaeum. The Romans, warned by Hiero of Syracuse of the coming raid, had time to intercept the Carthaginian contingent with a fleet of 20 quinqueremes and managed to capture several Carthaginian ships.

Bitka pri Lilibeju je bila prvi spopad med ladjevjema Kartagine in Rima leta 218 pr. n. št. v drugi punski vojni. Kartažani so poslali 35 kvinkerem, da bi plenile po Siciliji, začenši pri Lilibeju. Rimljane je pred napadom, ki je grozil, pravočasno posvaril Hieron iz Sirakuz, zato so imeli dovolj časa, da so z ladjevjem 20 kvinkerem prestregli kartažansko enoto in zajeli več njenih ladij.

events.label: Battle of Rhone Crossing
events.description: battle of the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of the Rhône Crossing
story.description: Battle of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of the Rhône Crossing was a battle during the Second Punic War in September of 218 BC. Hannibal marched on the Italian Alps, and an army of Gallic Volcae attacked the Carthaginian army on the east bank of the Rhône. The Roman army camped near Massalia. The Volcae tried to prevent the Carthaginians from crossing the Alps and invading Italy.

Before they crossed the river, the Carthaginians sent a detachment to cross upriver, under Hanno, son of Bomilcar, and took up position behind the Gauls. Once the detachment was in place, Hannibal crossed the river with the main contingent of his army. As the Gauls massed to oppose Hannibal, Hanno attacked their rear and routed the Volcae army. This was Hannibal's first major battle (victory) outside of the Iberian Peninsula. It gave him an unopposed path to the Alps and into Italy.

Bitka pri prečkanju Rone je potekala septembra 218 pr. n. št. med drugo punsko vojno. Hanibal je krenil proti italijanskim Alpam, vojska galskih Volkov pa je na vzhodnem bregu Rone napadla kartažansko vojsko. Rimska vojska je taborila blizu Massalije. Volki so skušali Kartažanom preprečiti, da bi prečkali Alpe in vdrli v Italijo.

Preden so prečkali reko, so Kartažani poslali odred pod vodstvom Hanona, Bomilkarjevega sina, da je reko prečkal više gor in se postavil za Galce. Ko je bil odred na položaju, je Hanibal reko prečkal z glavnino vojske. Ko so se Galci zbrali, da bi se Hanibalu postavili po robu, je Hanon napadel njihovo zaledje in vojsko Volkov pognal v beg. To je bila Hanibalova prva velika bitka (zmaga) zunaj Iberskega polotoka, ki mu je odprla nemoteno pot do Alp in v Italijo.

events.label: Battle of Ticinus
events.description: battle of the Second Punic War between the Carthaginian forces of Hannibal and the Romans under Publius Cornelius Scipio in November 218 BCE

story.title: Battle of Ticinus
story.description: Carthaginian-Roman battle, 218 BCE
paragraphs: The Battle of Ticinus was fought between the Carthaginian forces of Hannibal and a Roman army under Publius Cornelius Scipio in late November 218 BC as part of the Second Punic War. It took place in the flat country on the right bank of the river Ticinus, to the west of modern Pavia in northern Italy. Hannibal led 6,000 Libyan and Iberian cavalry, while Scipio led 3,600 Roman, Italian and Gallic cavalry and a large but unknown number of light infantry javelinmen.

War had been declared early in 218 BC over perceived infringements of Roman prerogatives in Iberia (modern Spain and Portugal) by Hannibal. Hannibal had gathered a large army, marched out of Iberia, through Gaul (modern France) and over the Alps into Cisalpine Gaul (northern Italy), where many of the local tribes were opposed to Rome. The Romans were taken by surprise, but one of the consuls for the year, Scipio, led an army along the north bank of the Po with the intention of giving battle to Hannibal. The two commanding generals each led out strong forces to reconnoitre their opponents. Scipio mixed many javelinmen with his main cavalry force, anticipating a large-scale skirmish. Hannibal put his close-order cavalry in the centre of his line, with his light Numidian cavalry on the wings.

On sighting the Roman infantry the Carthaginian centre immediately charged and the javelinmen fled back through the ranks of their cavalry. A large cavalry melee ensued: many cavalry dismounted to fight on foot and some of the Roman javelinmen reinforced the fighting line. This continued indecisively until the Numidians swept round both ends of the line of battle. They then attacked the still disorganised javelinmen; the small Roman cavalry reserve, to which Scipio had attached himself; and the rear of the already engaged Roman cavalry. All three of these Roman forces were thrown into confusion and panic.

Bitka pri Ticinu je potekala med kartažanskimi silami Hanibala in rimsko vojsko pod Publijem Kornelijem Scipionom konec novembra 218 pr. n. št. v drugi punski vojni. Bojevali so se na ravnini na desnem bregu reke Ticin, zahodno od današnje Pavie v severni Italiji. Hanibal je vodil 6000 libijskih in iberskih konjenikov, Scipion pa 3600 rimskih, italskih in galskih konjenikov ter veliko, a neznano število lahkih pehotnih metalcev kopij.

events.label: Battle of the Trebia
events.description: first major battle of the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of the Trebia
story.description: Battle of the Second Punic War, 218 BCE
paragraphs: The Battle of the Trebia (or Trebbia) was the first major battle of the Second Punic War, fought between the Carthaginian forces of Hannibal and a Roman army under Sempronius Longus on 22 or 23 December 218 BC. Each army had a strength of about 40,000 men; the Carthaginians were stronger in cavalry, the Romans in infantry. The battle took place on the flood plain of the west bank of the lower Trebia River, not far from the settlement of Placentia (modern Piacenza), and resulted in a heavy defeat for the Romans.

War broke out between Carthage and Rome in 218 BC. The leading Carthaginian general, Hannibal, responded by leading a large army out of Iberia (modern Spain and Portugal), through Gaul, across the Alps and into Cisalpine Gaul (in northern Italy). The Romans went on the attack against the reduced force which had survived the rigours of the march, and Publius Scipio personally led the cavalry and light infantry of the army he commanded against the Carthaginian cavalry at the Battle of Ticinus. The Romans were soundly beaten and Scipio was wounded. The Romans retreated to near Placentia, fortified their camp and awaited reinforcement. The Roman army in Sicily under Sempronius was redeployed to the north and joined with Scipio's force. After a day of heavy skirmishing in which the Romans gained the upper hand, Sempronius was eager for a battle.

events.label: Battle of Lake Trasimene
events.description: 217 BCE battle of the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Lake Trasimene
story.description: 217 BC battle of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of Lake Trasimene was fought when a Carthaginian force under Hannibal ambushed a Roman army commanded by Gaius Flaminius on 21 June 217 BC, during the Second Punic War. The battle took place on the north shore of Lake Trasimene, to the south of Cortona, and resulted in a heavy defeat for the Romans.

War had broken out between Rome and Carthage early in 218 BC. Hannibal, ruler of the Carthaginian territories in south-east Iberia, marched an army through Gaul, crossed the Alps and arrived in Cisalpine Gaul (northern Italy) later that year. The Romans rushed reinforcements north from Sicily but were badly defeated at the Battle of the Trebia.

The following spring, the Romans positioned an army on each side of the Apennine Mountains, but were surprised when a Carthaginian army more than 50,000 strong crossed the range by a difficult but unguarded route. The Carthaginians moved south into Etruria, plundering, razing the villages and killing all men encountered. Flaminius, in charge of the nearest Roman army, set off in pursuit. Hannibal arranged an ambush on the north shore of Lake Trasimene and trapped the Romans. With the Carthaginians attacking unexpectedly from the flank and the rear, possibly in poor visibility, there was no chance for the Romans to form even a rudimentary fighting line and they were defeated after three hours of hard fighting with 15,000 being killed. The trap failed to enclose the 6,000 Romans at the front of the column, who escaped; later in the day they were surrounded by pursuing Carthaginians and surrendered. Thus nearly all 25,000 Romans in Flaminius's army were killed or captured. This destruction of an entire army as a result of an ambush by another army is widely considered a unique occurrence. Several days later the Carthaginians wiped out the entire cavalry force of the second Roman army, who were not yet aware of the earlier disaster.

Bitka na Trasimenskem jezeru je potekala, ko je kartažanska vojska pod Hanibalom 21. junija 217 pr. n. št. v drugi punski vojni iz zasede napadla rimsko vojsko pod poveljstvom Gaja Flaminija. Bitka je potekala na severnem bregu Trasimenskega jezera, južno od Cortone, in se je končala s hudim porazom Rimljanov.

Vojna med Rimom in Kartagino je izbruhnila v začetku leta 218 pr. n. št. Hanibal, vladar kartažanskih ozemelj v jugovzhodni Iberiji, je vojsko popeljal skozi Galijo, prečkal Alpe in tistega leta pozneje prispel v Cisalpinsko Galijo (severna Italija). Rimljani so s Sicilije v naglici poslali okrepitve na sever, a so doživeli hud poraz v bitki pri Trebiji.

events.label: Battle of Ager Falernus
events.description: skirmish between the armies of Rome and Carthage during the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Ager Falernus
story.description: Military clash between Rome and Carthage
paragraphs: The Battle of Ager Falernus was a skirmish during the Second Punic War between the armies of Rome and Carthage. After winning the Battle of Lake Trasimene in Italy in 217 BC, the army commanded by Hannibal marched south and reached Campania. The Carthaginians ultimately moved into the district of Falernum, a fertile river valley surrounded by mountains.

Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus, who had been elected Roman dictator and commander of the Roman field forces after the disastrous defeat at Lake Trasimene, had dogged Hannibal and stuck to a strategy to fight only under favourable conditions. He now occupied all the river crossings and mountain passes leading out of the valley, thus blocking the Carthaginians inside.

After stripping the area of grain, cattle, and other supplies, Hannibal displayed brilliant tactics to provoke the Roman guard to leave one of the passes. Despite the protests of his staff officers, Fabius, who was camped near the pass with his main forces, refused to attack the Carthaginian army and it escaped the trap unscathed.

Bitka na Falernskem polju (Ager Falernus) je bila manjši spopad med vojskama Rima in Kartagine v drugi punski vojni. Po zmagi v bitki na Trasimenskem jezeru v Italiji leta 217 pr. n. št. je Hanibalova vojska odkorakala proti jugu in dosegla Kampanijo. Kartažani so se nazadnje premaknili v okrožje Falernum, rodovitno rečno dolino, obdano z gorami.

Kvint Fabij Maksim Verukoz, ki so ga po katastrofalnem porazu pri Trasimenskem jezeru izvolili za rimskega diktatorja in poveljnika rimskih poljskih sil, je Hanibala neprestano zasledoval in se držal strategije, da se bo boril le v ugodnih razmerah. Zdaj je zasedel vse rečne prehode in gorske prelaze, ki vodijo iz doline, in tako Kartažane ujel vanjo.

Potem ko je območje opustošil in mu pobral žito, živino in druge zaloge, je Hanibal z briljantno taktiko poskušal rimsko stražo zvabiti z enega od prelazov. Kljub protestom svojih častnikov se Fabij, ki je s svojimi glavnimi silami taboril blizu prelaza, ni hotel spopasti s kartažansko vojsko, ta pa je pasti ušla nepoškodovana.

events.label: Battle of Ebro River
events.description: naval battle of the Second Punic War, fought near the mouth of Ebro River in the spring of 217 BC

story.title: Battle of Ebro River
story.description: 217 BC naval battle between the Romans and the Carthaginians
paragraphs: The Battle of Ebro River was a naval battle fought near the mouth of Ebro River in the spring of 217 BC between a Carthaginian fleet of approximately 40 quinqueremes, under the command of Himilco, and a Roman fleet of 35 ships, under Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Calvus. Hasdrubal Barca, the Carthaginian commander in Iberia, had launched a joint expedition to destroy the Roman base north of the Ebro River. The Carthaginian naval contingent was totally defeated after a surprise attack by the Roman ships, losing 29 ships and the control of seas around Iberia. The reputation of the Romans was further enhanced in Iberia after this victory, causing rebellion among some of the Iberian tribes under Carthaginian control.

Bitka pri reki Ebro je bila pomorska bitka spomladi 217 pr. n. št. blizu ustja reke Ebro med kartažanskim ladjevjem s približno 40 kvinkveremami pod poveljstvom Himilka in rimskim ladjevjem s 35 ladjami pod Gnejem Kornelijem Scipionom Kalvom. Hasdrubal Barka, kartažanski poveljnik na Iberskem polotoku, je sprožil skupen pohod, da bi uničil rimsko oporišče severno od reke Ebro. Kartažanski pomorski oddelek je bil po presenetljivem napadu rimskih ladij popolnoma poražen: izgubil je 29 ladij in nadzor nad morji okoli Iberskega polotoka. Po tej zmagi je ugled Rimljanov na Iberskem polotoku še zrasel, zato so se uprla nekatera iberska plemena pod kartažansko oblastjo.

events.label: Battle of Geronium
events.description: battle of the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Geronium
story.description: Battle of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of Geronium (also spelled Gerunium) was a significant engagement fought between the forces of Carthage and the Roman Republic during the summer and autumn of 217 BC, amid the broader context of the Second Punic War. The confrontation resulted in a tactical victory for the Carthaginian general Hannibal Barca, consolidating his position in southern Italy and further undermining Roman morale.

Following his successful maneuvering in the Battle of Ager Falernus, Hannibal led his army northward before turning east toward Molise, passing through the rugged terrain of Samnium. Throughout this movement, he was shadowed by Roman forces under the command of Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus, who continued to implement his strategy of attrition—later known as the Fabian strategy—deliberately avoiding pitched battle with Hannibal's superior tactical forces.

Fabius's cautious approach, while militarily prudent, was politically unpopular in Rome. Facing criticism, he temporarily returned to the city under the pretense of performing religious duties, leaving his second-in-command, Marcus Minucius Rufus, in operational control.

During Fabius's absence, Minucius launched an aggressive attack on a Carthaginian detachment near Geronium, inflicting notable losses and killing approximately 5,000 enemy troops in what was likely a large-scale skirmish. This perceived success won Minucius popular support in Rome, leading the Senate to elevate him to equal authority with Fabius—a rare dual command structure in Roman military tradition.

Minucius, now operating independently, took control of half the Roman forces and established a separate camp near Geronium. Seizing the opportunity, Hannibal devised an elaborate ambush, exploiting Minucius's overconfidence. He drew out the Roman forces and launched a coordinated attack, enveloping Minucius's detachment. The intervention of Fabius with the remaining Roman forces prevented a complete rout, but the Romans suffered substantial casualties.

Bitka pri Geroniumu (zapisana tudi Gerunium) je bila pomemben spopad med silami Kartagine in Rimske republike poleti in jeseni 217 pr. n. št. v širšem okviru druge punske vojne. Spopad se je končal s taktično zmago kartažanskega poveljnika Hanibala Barke, ki je utrdila njegov položaj v južni Italiji in dodatno spodkopala rimski moral.

Po uspešnem manevriranju v bitki na Falernskem polju je Hanibal vojsko popeljal proti severu, nato pa zavil proti vzhodu, proti Moliseju, in prečkal razgiban svet Samnija. Ves ta čas so ga zasledovale rimske sile pod poveljstvom Kvinta Fabija Maksima Verukoza, ki je še naprej izvajal svojo strategijo izčrpavanja, pozneje znano kot fabijska strategija, in se namenoma izogibal odprti bitki s Hanibalovimi taktično boljšimi silami.

events.label: Battle of Nola
events.description: 216 BCE battle of the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Nola (216 BC)
story.description: 216 BC battle of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The First Battle of Nola was fought in 216 BC between the forces of Hannibal and a Roman force led by Marcus Claudius Marcellus. Hannibal was attempting to seize the town of Nola: He failed to do so, and would make two more unsuccessful attempts on the city over the next two years.

Hannibal moved to capture the city of Nola due to some leaders in the city offering to open their gates to him. A Roman force under the command of Marcellus arrived before Hannibal and was able to enter the city. Hannibal camped near the city, and daily skirmishes took place between the two armies. Marcellus learnt that the only support he enjoyed was the senators in the city. Marcellus took action to prevent betrayal by undermining the pro-Hannibal faction in the city. Marcellus learnt that some leaders in the city had been conspiring with Hannibal, and he discovered that should he make any sortie from the town or draw up for battle outside, they planned on plundering the baggage and closing the gates behind him. After this, Marcellus decided his situation was not sustainable.

Prva bitka pri Noli je potekala leta 216 pr. n. št. med Hanibalovimi silami in rimskimi silami pod poveljstvom Marka Klavdija Marcela. Hanibal je skušal mesto Nolo zavzeti, a mu ni uspelo, v naslednjih dveh letih pa je poskusil še dvakrat, prav tako neuspešno.

Hanibal je mesto Nolo skušal zavzeti, ker so mu nekateri mestni voditelji ponudili, da mu odprejo vrata. Rimske sile pod Marcelovim poveljstvom so prispele pred Hanibalom in so lahko vstopile v mesto. Hanibal se je utaboril blizu mesta, med vojskama pa so bile vsak dan praske. Marcel je ugotovil, da mu v mestu pomagajo samo senatorji. Da bi preprečil izdajo, je začel spodkopavati Hanibalu naklonjeno frakcijo v mestu. Izvedel je, da so nekateri voditelji mesta kovali zaroto s Hanibalom, in odkril, da so načrtovali, da bi oplenili njegovo prtljago in za njim zaprli vrata, če bi naredil izpad iz mesta ali se zunaj postavil v bojni red. Po tem je Marcel presodil, da njegov položaj ni vzdržen.

events.label: Battle of Cannae
events.description: major battle of the Second Punic War (216 BCE)

story.title: Battle of Cannae
story.description: Largest battle of the Second Punic War (216 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Cannae (Latin: [ˈkanːae̯]) was a key engagement of the Second Punic War between the Roman Republic and Carthage, fought on 2 August 216 BC near the ancient village of Cannae in Apulia, southeast Italy. The Carthaginians and their allies, led by Hannibal, surrounded and practically annihilated a larger Roman and Italian army under the consuls Lucius Aemilius Paullus and Gaius Terentius Varro. It is regarded as one of the greatest tactical feats in military history and one of the worst defeats in Roman history, and it cemented Hannibal's reputation as one of antiquity's greatest tacticians.

Having recovered from their losses at Trebia (218 BC) and Lake Trasimene (217 BC), the Romans decided to engage Hannibal at Cannae, with approximately 86,000 Roman and allied socii troops. They massed their heavy infantry in a deeper formation than usual, while Hannibal used the double envelopment tactic and surrounded his enemy, trapping the majority of the Roman army, who were then slaughtered. Later historians and military strategists have used Cannae as an exemplary battle of annihilation. The loss of life on the Roman side meant it was one of the most lethal single days of fighting in history; historian Adrian Goldsworthy equates the death toll at Cannae to "the massed slaughter of the British Army on the first day of the Somme offensive in 1916". Only about 15,000 Romans, most of whom were from the garrisons of the camps and had not taken part in the battle, survived. Following the defeat, Capua and several other Italian city-states defected from the Roman Republic to Carthage.

events.label: Battle of Cornus
events.description: battle of the Second Punic War, taking place when a Carthaginian army sailed to Sardinia in support of a Sardinian revolt against Roman rule

story.title: Battle of Decimomannu
story.description: Roman victory during the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of Decimomannu, Battle of Cornus or Battle of Caralis was fought 215 BC on the island of Sardinia when a Carthaginian army sailed to the island to support a local revolt against Roman rule. The army, led by Hasdrubal the Bald, fought a Roman army of similar size under the praetor Titus Manlius Torquatus in the Fall of 215 BC somewhere between Sestu and Decimomannu, just north of Caralis. The Romans destroyed the Carthaginian army and then scattered their fleet in a sea battle south of Sardinia.

Bitka pri Decimomannu, bitka pri Cornusu ali bitka pri Caralisu je potekala leta 215 pr. n. št. na otoku Sardiniji, ko je kartažanska vojska priplula na otok, da bi podprla krajevni upor proti rimski oblasti. Vojska pod poveljstvom Hasdrubala Plešastega se je jeseni 215 pr. n. št. nekje med krajema Sestu in Decimomannu, tik severno od Caralisa, spopadla z rimsko vojsko podobne velikosti pod pretorjem Titom Manlijem Torkvatom. Rimljani so kartažansko vojsko uničili, nato pa v pomorski bitki južno od Sardinije razpršili še njeno ladjevje.

events.label: Battle of Dertosa
events.description: "battle of the Second Punic War, fought in the spring of 215 BCE on the south bank of the Ebro River across from the town of Dertosa",battle

story.title: Battle of Ibera
story.description: Battle of the Second Punic War, fought in Spain
paragraphs: The Battle of Ibera, also known as the Battle of Dertosa, was fought in the spring of 215 BC on the south bank of the Ebro River near the town of Ibera and was part of the Second Punic War. A Roman army, under the command of the brothers Gnaeus and Publius Scipio, defeated a similarly sized Carthaginian army under Hasdrubal Barca. The Romans, under Gnaeus Scipio, had invaded Iberia in late 218 BC and established a foothold after winning the Battle of Cissa. This lodgement, on the north-east Iberian coast, between the Ebro and the Pyrenees, blocked the route of any reinforcements from Iberia for the army of Hannibal, who had invaded Italy from Iberia earlier in the year. Hasdrubal attempted to evict the Romans in 217 BC, but this ended in defeat when the Carthaginian naval contingent was mauled at the Battle of Ebro River.

Hasdrubal spent the rest of 217 BC and all of 216 BC subduing rebellious indigenous Iberian tribes, largely in the south. Under pressure from Carthage to reinforce Hannibal, and having been strongly reinforced, Hasdrubal marched north again in early 215 BC. Meanwhile, Scipio, who had also been reinforced, and joined by his brother Publius, had crossed the Ebro to besiege the Carthaginian-aligned town of Ibera. Hasdrubal approached and offered battle, which the Scipios accepted. Both armies were of similar sizes, about 25,000 men. When they clashed, the centre of Hasdrubal's army – which consisted of locally recruited Iberians – fled without fighting. The Roman legions pushed through the gap, turned to each side against the remaining Carthaginian infantry and enveloped them. Both sides are reported to have suffered heavy casualties; the Carthaginians' may have been very heavy. The Carthaginian camp was sacked, but Hasdrubal escaped with most of his cavalry.

Bitka pri Iberi, znana tudi kot bitka pri Dertosi, je potekala spomladi 215 pr. n. št. na južnem bregu reke Ebro blizu mesta Ibera in je bila del druge punske vojne. Rimska vojska pod poveljstvom bratov Gneja in Publija Scipiona je premagala podobno veliko kartažansko vojsko pod Hasdrubalom Barko. Rimljani pod Gnejem Scipionom so konec leta 218 pr. n. št. vdrli na Iberski polotok in si po zmagi v bitki pri Cissi ustvarili oporišče. To oporišče na severovzhodni iberski obali med Ebrom in Pireneji je zapiralo pot vsem okrepitvam z Iberskega polotoka za vojsko Hanibala, ki je v začetku tistega leta z Iberskega polotoka vdrl v Italijo. Hasdrubal je Rimljane skušal pregnati leta 217 pr. n. št., a se je to končalo s porazom, ko je bil kartažanski pomorski oddelek uničen v bitki pri reki Ebro.

events.label: Battle of Nola
events.description: 215 BCE battle of the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Nola (215 BC)
story.description: 215 BC battle of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Second Battle of Nola was fought in 215 BC between Hannibal's army and a Roman force under Marcus Claudius Marcellus. It was Hannibal's second attempt to seize Nola after a failure the year before. He was again repelled and would make one more, also unsuccessful attempt the next year. For the Romans, it was a crucial success against Hannibal's army and gave them hope that they could win the war.

Druga bitka pri Noli je potekala leta 215 pr. n. št. med Hanibalovo vojsko in rimskimi silami pod poveljstvom Marka Klavdija Marcela. Hanibal je Nolo po neuspehu prejšnjega leta skušal zavzeti drugič. Spet so ga odbili, naslednje leto pa je poskusil še zadnjič, prav tako neuspešno. Za Rimljane je bil to ključen uspeh proti Hanibalovi vojski, ki jim je dal upanje, da lahko vojno dobijo.

events.label: Battle of Beneventum
events.description: battle fought in 214 BCE near modern Benevento during the Second Punic War, in which Roman legions under Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus defeated Hanno's Carthaginian forces, denying Hannibal reinforcements
events.sl: Bitka pri Beneventu leta 214 pr. n. št.

story.title: Battle of Beneventum (214 BC)
story.description: Roman victory in the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of Beneventum was fought in 214 BC near modern Benevento during the Second Punic War. Roman legions under Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus defeated Hanno's Carthaginian forces, denying Hannibal reinforcements. Livy gives a brief description of the battle, which was part of the Roman campaign to subdue the southern Italian city-states that had joined Hannibal after the Battle of Cannae.

Bitka pri Beneventu je potekala leta 214 pr. n. št. blizu današnjega Beneventa v drugi punski vojni. Rimske legije pod Tiberijem Sempronijem Grakhom so porazile kartažanske sile pod Hanonom in Hanibalu preprečile okrepitve. Livij bitko na kratko opisuje; bila je del rimske kampanje za podreditev južnoitalijanskih mestnih držav, ki so se po bitki pri Kanah pridružile Hanibalu.

events.label: Battle of Nola
events.description: 214 BCE battle of the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Nola (214 BC)
story.description: 214 BC battle of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Third Battle of Nola was fought in 214 BC between Hannibal and a Roman army led by Marcus Claudius Marcellus. It was Hannibal's third attempt to take the town of Nola. Once again, Marcellus successfully prevented the town's capture.

Tretja bitka pri Noli je potekala leta 214 pr. n. št. med Hanibalom in rimsko vojsko pod poveljstvom Marka Klavdija Marcela. Hanibal je mesto Nolo skušal zavzeti že tretjič. Marcel je spet uspešno preprečil njeno zavzetje.

events.label: Siege of Syracuse
events.description: 214-212 BCE siege of the Second Punic War ending in the fall of the Hellenistic city of Syracuse to the Roman Republic

story.title: Siege of Syracuse (213–212 BC)
story.description: Roman victory during the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The siege of Syracuse by the Roman Republic took place in 213–212 BC. The Romans successfully stormed the Hellenistic city of Syracuse after a protracted siege, giving them control of the entire island of Sicily. During the siege, the city was protected by weapons developed by the prominent inventor and polymath Archimedes, who was slain at the conclusion of the siege by a Roman soldier, in contravention of the Roman proconsul Marcellus's instructions to spare his life.

Rimska republika je Sirakuze oblegala v letih 213–212 pr. n. št. Po dolgem obleganju so Rimljani helenistično mesto Sirakuze uspešno zavzeli z naskokom in tako dobili nadzor nad vso Sicilijo. Med obleganjem so mesto varovala orožja, ki jih je razvil znameniti izumitelj in polihistor Arhimed, na koncu obleganja pa ga je ubil rimski vojak, v nasprotju z navodili rimskega prokonzula Marcela, naj mu prizanesejo življenje.

events.label: Battle of Capua
events.description: battle of the Second Punic War in 212 BCE where Hannibal defeated two Roman consular armies and temporarily managed to raise the siege of Capua

story.title: Battle of Capua (212 BC)
story.description: 212 BC battle
paragraphs: The First Battle of Capua was fought in 212 BC between Hannibal Barca and two Roman consular armies. The Roman force was led by two consuls, Quintus Fulvius Flaccus and Appius Claudius Pulcher. The Roman force was defeated, but managed to escape. Hannibal temporarily managed to raise the siege of Capua. A tactical Carthaginian victory, it ultimately did not help the Capuans.

Prva bitka pri Capui je potekala leta 212 pr. n. št. med Hanibalom Barko in dvema rimskima konzularnima vojskama. Rimsko vojsko sta vodila konzula Kvint Fulvij Flak in Apij Klavdij Pulher. Rimska vojska je bila poražena, a ji je uspelo pobegniti. Hanibalu je začasno uspelo prekiniti obleganje Capue. Čeprav je bila to taktična kartažanska zmaga, Capuancem nazadnje ni pomagala.

events.label: Battle of Herdonia
events.description: 212 BCE battle of the Second Punic War in which Hannibal's Carthaginian army destroyed a Roman army led by Praetor Gnaeus Fulvius Flaccus

story.title: Battle of Herdonia (212 BC)
story.description: Battle of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The first Battle of Herdonia was fought in 212 BC during the Second Punic War between Hannibal's Carthaginian army and Roman forces led by Praetor Gnaeus Fulvius Flaccus, brother of the consul Quintus Fulvius Flaccus. The Roman army was destroyed, leaving Apulia free of Romans for the year.

Prva bitka pri Herdoniji je potekala leta 212 pr. n. št. v drugi punski vojni med Hanibalovo kartažansko vojsko in rimskimi silami pod vodstvom pretorja Gneja Fulvija Flaka, brata konzula Kvinta Fulvija Flaka. Rimska vojska je bila uničena, zato je bila Apulija tisto leto brez Rimljanov.

events.label: Battle of the Silarus
events.description: 212 BCE battle of the Second Punic War in which Hannibal's army destroyed a Roman army led by praetor Marcus Centenius Penula
events.sl: Bitka pri Silarusu leta 212 pr. n. št.

story.title: Battle of the Silarus
story.description: 212 BC victory of Hannibal's army
paragraphs: The Battle of the Silarus was fought in 212 BC between Hannibal's army and a Roman force led by centurion Marcus Centenius Penula. The vastly outnumbered Carthaginians were victorious, destroying the entire Roman army and killing 15,000 Roman soldiers in the process.

Bitka pri Silarusu je potekala leta 212 pr. n. št. med Hanibalovo vojsko in rimskimi silami pod poveljstvom stotnika Marka Centenija Penule. Kartažani, ki so bili v veliki številčni manjšini, so zmagali: uničili so vso rimsko vojsko in pri tem ubili 15.000 rimskih vojakov.

events.label: Battle of Capua
events.description: battle of the Second Punic War that took place in 211 BCE when the Romans besieged and captured Capua

story.title: Siege of Capua (211 BC)
story.description: 211 BC battle of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Siege of Capua was fought in 211 BC, when the Romans besieged Capua. It is described by Polybius at 9.4–7, by Livy at 26.4–6, and by Appian at 37–44 of his Hannibalic War.
Obleganje Capue je potekalo leta 211 pr. n. št., ko so Rimljani oblegali Capuo. Opisujejo ga Polibij v 9.4–7, Livij v 26.4–6 in Apijan v 37–44 svojega dela Hanibalova vojna.

events.label: Battle of the Upper Baetis
events.description: double battle, battles of Castulo and Ilorca, fought in 211 BCE between Rome and Carthage

story.title: Battle of the Upper Baetis
story.description: 211 BCE battle during the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of the Upper Baetis was a double battle, comprising the battles of Castulo and Ilorca, fought in 211 BC during the Second Punic War between a Carthaginian force led by Hasdrubal Barca (Hannibal's brother) and a Roman force led by Publius Cornelius Scipio and his brother Gnaeus. The immediate result was a Carthaginian victory in which both Roman brothers were killed. Before this defeat, the brothers had spent seven years (218–211 BC) campaigning against the Carthaginians in Hispania, thus limiting the resources available to Hannibal, who was simultaneously fighting the Romans in Italy.

Bitka ob gornjem Baetisu je bila dvojna bitka, sestavljena iz bitk pri Kastulu in Ilorki, ki je potekala leta 211 pr. n. št. v drugi punski vojni med kartažanskimi silami pod vodstvom Hasdrubala Barke (Hanibalovega brata) in rimskimi silami pod vodstvom Publija Kornelija Scipiona in njegovega brata Gneja. Neposredni izid je bila kartažanska zmaga, v kateri sta padla oba rimska brata. Pred tem porazom sta se brata sedem let (218–211 pr. n. št.) bojevala proti Kartažanom v Hispaniji in tako omejevala vire, ki so bili na voljo Hanibalu, ki se je hkrati bojeval z Rimljani v Italiji.

events.label: Battle of Herdonia
events.description: 210 BCE battle of the Second Punic War in which Hannibal's Carthaginians encircled and destroyed a Roman army which was operating against his allies in Apulia

story.title: Battle of Herdonia (210 BC)
story.description: 210 BC battle in the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The second battle of Herdonia took place in 210 BC during the Second Punic War. Hannibal, leader of the Carthaginians, who had invaded Italy eight years earlier, encircled and destroyed a Roman army which was operating against his allies in Apulia. The heavy defeat increased the war's burden on Rome and, piled on previous military disasters (such as Lake Trasimene, Cannae, and others), aggravated the relations with her exhausted Italian allies. For Hannibal the battle was a tactical success, but did not halt for long the Roman advance. Within the next three years the Romans reconquered most of the territories and cities lost at the beginning of the war and pushed the Carthaginian general to the southwestern end of the Apennine Peninsula.

Druga bitka pri Herdoniji je potekala leta 210 pr. n. št. v drugi punski vojni. Hanibal, vodja Kartažanov, ki je v Italijo vdrl osem let prej, je obkolil in uničil rimsko vojsko, ki je delovala proti njegovim zaveznikom v Apuliji. Težki poraz je povečal breme vojne za Rim in skupaj s prejšnjimi vojaškimi katastrofami (kot so bile Trasimensko jezero, Kane in druge) poslabšal odnose z izčrpanimi italijanskimi zavezniki. Za Hanibala je bila bitka taktičen uspeh, vendar rimskega napredovanja ni za dolgo ustavila. V naslednjih treh letih so Rimljani ponovno osvojili večino ozemelj in mest, izgubljenih na začetku vojne, in kartažanskega poveljnika potisnili na jugozahodni konec Apeninskega polotoka.

events.label: Battle of Numistro
events.description: battle of the Second Punic War ending in a stalemate between Hannibal's army and a Roman consular army led by consul Marcus Claudius Marcellus

story.title: Battle of Numistro
story.description: 210 BC stalemate between Hannibal and Rome
paragraphs: The Battle of Numistro was fought in 210 BC between Hannibal's army and one of the Roman consular armies led by consul Marcus Claudius Marcellus.
