It was the fourth time they met in a battle. Previous encounters were located around the walls of Nola (Campania) in 216, 215, and 214 and had been favourable for the Roman side.

Bitka pri Numistru je potekala leta 210 pr. n. št. med Hanibalovo vojsko in eno od rimskih konzularnih vojsk pod vodstvom konzula Marka Klavdija Marcela. Bila je njuno četrto srečanje v bitki. Prejšnja srečanja so potekala ob obzidju Nole (Kampanija) leta 216, 215 in 214 pr. n. št. in so bila za Rimljane ugodna.

events.label: Battle of Canusium
events.description: battle of the Second Punic War consisting in a three-day engagement in Apulia, Italy between the forces of Rome and Carthage in the summer of 209 BCE

story.title: Battle of Canusium
story.description: Battle in 209 BCE
paragraphs: The Battle of Canusium also known as the Battle of Asculum was a three-day engagement between the forces of Rome and Carthage. It took place in Apulia during the spring of 209 BC, the tenth year of the Second Punic War. A larger Roman offensive, of which it was a part, aimed to subjugate and to punish cities and tribes that had abandoned the alliance with Rome after the Battle of Cannae, and to narrow the base of the Carthaginian leader, Hannibal, in southern Italy.

The battle of Canusium was also an episode of the years-long contest between Hannibal and the Roman general Marcus Claudius Marcellus for control over that territory. As neither side gained a decisive victory and both suffered considerable losses (up to 14,000 killed overall), the outcome of this engagement was open to differing interpretations by both ancient and modern historians. While Marcellus took a heavy blow at Canusium, he nevertheless checked for some time the movements of the main Punic forces and thus contributed to the simultaneous Roman successes against Hannibal's allies in Magna Graecia and Lucania.

Bitka pri Canusiumu, znana tudi kot bitka pri Askulu, je bila tridnevni spopad med silami Rima in Kartagine. Potekal je v Apuliji spomladi 209 pr. n. št., v desetem letu druge punske vojne. Bila je del večje rimske ofenzive, katere cilj je bil podjarmiti in kaznovati mesta in plemena, ki so po bitki pri Kanah zapustila zavezništvo z Rimom, ter zožiti oporišče kartažanskega vodje Hanibala v južni Italiji.

Bitka pri Canusiumu je bila tudi epizoda dolgoletnega boja za nadzor nad tem ozemljem med Hanibalom in rimskim poveljnikom Markom Klavdijem Marcelom. Ker nobena stran ni dosegla odločilne zmage in sta obe utrpeli znatne izgube (skupaj do 14.000 mrtvih), so lahko antični in sodobni zgodovinarji izid te bitke razlagali različno. Čeprav je Marcel pri Canusiumu doživel hud udarec, je vendarle za nekaj časa zaustavil gibanje glavnih punskih sil in tako prispeval k hkratnim rimskim uspehom proti Hanibalovim zaveznikom v Veliki Grčiji in Lukaniji.

events.label: Battle of New Carthage
events.description: 209 BCE successful Roman assault on the Carthaginian stronghold New Carthage (Cartagena) in Iberia

story.title: Battle of New Carthage
story.description: 209 BC battle of the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The battle of New Carthage took place in early 209 BC when a Roman army under Publius Cornelius Scipio successfully assaulted New Carthage, the capital of Carthaginian Iberia, which was defended by a garrison under Mago. The battle was part of the Second Punic War.

In 211 BC the Romans in Iberia (modern Spain and Portugal) were heavily defeated at the battle of the Upper Baetis. Reinforcements arrived in early 210 BC and Scipio brought further reinforcements when he took command late in the year. Scipio felt unable to draw into battle and defeat any of the three strong Carthaginian armies in the peninsula and so decided to strike at the material centre of Carthaginian power in Iberia: its capital, New Carthage. He arrived outside the city early in 209 BC and commenced his attack the next day. After defeating a Carthaginian force outside the walls, he pressed an attack on the east gate. Simultaneously men from the Roman ships attempted to escalade the wall to the south from the harbour area. Both attacks were repulsed.

In the afternoon Scipio renewed the attacks. Hard-pressed, Mago moved men from the north wall, which overlooked a broad, shallow lagoon. Anticipating this, Scipio sent a force of 500 men through the lagoon to scale the north wall, which they did unopposed. They fought their way to the east gate, opened it from inside and let in their comrades. New Carthage fell and was sacked, and Mago surrendered the citadel and the last of his troops. Vast amounts of precious metal and war materiel were seized. New Carthage became the logistics centre of the Roman war effort in Iberia and by 206 BC the Carthaginians had been expelled from the peninsula.

Bitka za Novo Kartagino je potekala v začetku leta 209 pr. n. št., ko je rimska vojska pod Publijem Kornelijem Scipionom uspešno naskočila Novo Kartagino, prestolnico kartažanske Iberije, ki jo je branila posadka pod Magonom. Bitka je bila del druge punske vojne.

Leta 211 pr. n. št. so Rimljani na Iberskem polotoku (današnji Španiji in Portugalski) doživeli hud poraz v bitki ob gornjem Baetisu. Okrepitve so prispele v začetku leta 210 pr. n. št., nove pa je pripeljal Scipion, ko je konec leta prevzel poveljstvo. Scipion ni videl možnosti, da bi katero od treh močnih kartažanskih vojsk na polotoku zvabil v bitko in jo premagal, zato se je odločil udariti na materialno središče kartažanske moči na Iberskem polotoku: njeno prestolnico Novo Kartagino. Pred mesto je prispel v začetku leta 209 pr. n. št. in naslednji dan začel napad. Ko je pred obzidjem premagal kartažanski oddelek, je napadel vzhodna vrata. Hkrati so se možje z rimskih ladij s pristaniškega območja skušali povzpeti na obzidje na jugu. Oba napada so odbili.

events.label: Battle of Baecula
events.description: Scipio Africanus’s first major field battle after he had taken command of Roman interests in Iberia during the Second Punic War, in which he routed the Carthaginian army under the command of Hasdrubal Barca

story.title: Battle of Baecula
story.description: Battle in Iberia during the Second Punic War (208 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Baecula was a major field battle in Iberia during the Second Punic War. Roman Republican and Iberian auxiliary forces under the command of Scipio Africanus routed the Carthaginian army of Hasdrubal Barca.

Bitka pri Baeculi je bila velika bitka na Iberskem polotoku v drugi punski vojni. Rimske republikanske sile in iberske pomožne enote pod poveljstvom Scipiona Afriškega so pognale v beg kartažansko vojsko Hasdrubala Barke.

events.label: Battle of Grumentum
events.description: 207 BCE battle of the Second Punic War in which the Romans led by Gaius Claudius Nero won a minor victory over a part of Hannibal's Carthaginian army

story.title: Battle of Grumentum
story.description: 207 BCE battle
paragraphs: The Battle of Grumentum was fought in 207 BC between Romans led by Gaius Claudius Nero, and a part of Hannibal's Carthaginian army. The battle was a minor engagement that Roman sources inflated as a major success. According to Livy, the Romans killed 8,000 Carthaginians and took 700 prisoners for the cost of 500 dead Romans. The Carthaginian loss figures for dead and prisoners appear suspiciously out of proportion to each other. Just north of the battlefield the next day, an irregular clash occurred where allegedly another 2,000 Carthaginians were killed. Afterwards, Nero marched north, where he defeated and killed Hannibal's brother Hasdrubal at Metaurus. The battle is described by Livy at 27.41–42.

Bitka pri Grumentumu je potekala leta 207 pr. n. št. med Rimljani pod vodstvom Gaja Klavdija Nerona in delom Hanibalove kartažanske vojske. Bila je manjši spopad, ki so ga rimski viri napihnili v veliko zmago. Po Liviju so Rimljani pobili 8000 Kartažanov in jih ujeli 700, sami pa so izgubili 500 mož. Števili kartažanskih mrtvih in ujetih sta videti sumljivo neskladni. Naslednji dan je tik severno od bojišča prišlo do neurejenega spopada, v katerem naj bi bilo ubitih še 2000 Kartažanov. Nato je Neron odkorakal proti severu, kjer je na Metavru premagal in ubil Hanibalovega brata Hasdrubala. Livij jo opisuje v 27.41–42.

events.label: Battle of the Metaurus
events.description: pivotal battle in the Second Punic War between Rome and Carthage, fought in 207 BCE near the Metauro River in present-day Italy

story.title: Battle of the Metaurus
story.description: 207 BC battle during the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of the Metaurus was a pivotal battle in the Second Punic War between Rome and Carthage, fought in 207 BC near the Metauro River in Italy. The Carthaginians were led by Hasdrubal Barca, brother of Hannibal, who was to have brought siege equipment and reinforcements for Hannibal. The Roman armies were led by the consuls Marcus Livius, who was later nicknamed the Salinator, and Gaius Claudius Nero.

Claudius Nero had just fought Hannibal in Grumentum, some hundreds of kilometres south of the Metaurus river, and reached Marcus Livius by a forced march that went unnoticed by both Hannibal and Hasdrubal, so that the Carthaginians suddenly found themselves outnumbered. In the battle, the Romans used their numerical superiority to outflank the Carthaginian army and rout them, the Carthaginians losing 15,400 men killed or captured, including Hasdrubal.

The battle confirmed Roman supremacy over Italy. Without Hasdrubal's army to support him, Hannibal was compelled to evacuate pro-Carthaginian towns in much of southern Italy in the face of Roman pressure and withdraw to Bruttium, where he would remain for the next four years.

Bitka na Metavru je bila prelomna bitka v drugi punski vojni med Rimom in Kartagino, ki je potekala leta 207 pr. n. št. blizu reke Metaver (italijansko Metauro) v Italiji. Kartažane je vodil Hasdrubal Barka, Hanibalov brat, ki bi moral Hanibalu prinesti obleganjsko opremo in okrepitve. Rimski vojski sta vodila konzula Mark Livij, ki so mu pozneje nadeli vzdevek Salinator, in Gaj Klavdij Neron.

Klavdij Neron se je pravkar spopadel s Hanibalom pri Grumentumu, nekaj sto kilometrov južno od reke Metaver, in je do Marka Livija prispel s prisilnim pohodom, ki ga ni opazil ne Hanibal ne Hasdrubal, tako da so se Kartažani nenadoma znašli v številčni podrejenosti. V bitki so Rimljani s številčno premočjo obšli kartažansko vojsko in jo razbili, Kartažani pa so izgubili 15.400 mož, mrtvih ali ujetih, med njimi Hasdrubala.

events.label: Battle of Ilipa
events.description: Scipio Africanus’s most brilliant victory in his military career during the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Ilipa
story.description: 206 BC Second Punic War Roman victory in Spain
paragraphs: The Battle of Ilipa was an engagement considered by many as Scipio Africanus's most brilliant victory in his military career during the Second Punic War in 206 BC. It may have taken place on a plain east of Alcalá del Río, Seville, Spain, near the village of Esquivel, the site of the Carthaginian camp.

Though it may not seem to be as original as Hannibal's tactic at Cannae, Scipio's pre-battle maneuver and his reverse Cannae formation stands as the acme of his tactical ability, in which he permanently broke the Carthaginian grip and source of power in Iberia, thus denying any further land invasion into Italy and cutting off a rich base for the Barca dynasty both in silver and manpower.

Bitka pri Ilipi je bila spopad leta 206 pr. n. št. v drugi punski vojni, ki ga mnogi štejejo za najsijajnejšo zmago v vojaški karieri Scipiona Afriškega. Morda je potekala na ravnini vzhodno od kraja Alcalá del Río pri Sevilli v Španiji, blizu vasi Esquivel, kjer je bil kartažanski tabor.

Čeprav se morda ne zdi tako izvirna kot Hanibalova taktika pri Kanah, sta Scipionov manever pred bitko in njegova obrnjena formacija »Kane« vrhunec njegove taktične spretnosti: z njima je dokončno strl kartažanski nadzor in vir moči na Iberskem polotoku ter tako preprečil vsak nadaljnji kopenski vdor v Italijo in rodbini Barka odrezal bogato zaledje srebra in ljudi.

events.label: Battle of Crotona
events.description: one of the last larger scale engagements between the Romans and the Carthaginians in Italy during the Second Punic War

story.title: Battles of Kroton
story.description: Battles in 204 and 203 BC
paragraphs: The Battles of Kroton in 204 and 203 BC were, as well as the raid in Cisalpine Gaul, the last larger scale engagements between the Romans and the Carthaginians in Italy during the Second Punic War. After Hannibal’s retreat to Bruttium due to the Metaurus debacle, the Romans continuously tried to block his forces from gaining access to the Ionian Sea and cut his eventual escape to Carthage by capturing Kroton, the last port which had remained in his hands after years of fighting.

Bitki pri Krotonu (Crotone) v letih 204 in 203 pr. n. št. sta bili poleg plenilnega pohoda v Cisalpinski Galiji zadnja večja spopada med Rimljani in Kartažani v Italiji med drugo punsko vojno. Po Hanibalovem umiku v Brutij zaradi poraza na Metavru so Rimljani nenehno poskušali preprečiti, da bi njegove sile dosegle Jonsko morje, in prekiniti njegov morebitni pobeg v Kartagino, in sicer z zavzetjem Krotona, zadnjega pristanišča, ki je ostalo v njegovih rokah po letih bojev.

events.label: Battle of Utica
events.description: 203 BCE battle of the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Utica (203 BC)
story.description: Battle of the Second Punic War in 203 BC
paragraphs: The battle of Utica was fought in 203 BC between a Roman army commanded by Publius Cornelius Scipio and the allied armies of Carthage and Numidia, commanded by Hasdrubal Gisgo and Syphax respectively. The battle was part of the Second Punic War and resulted in a heavy defeat for Carthage.

In the wake of its defeat in the First Punic War (264–241 BC) Carthage expanded its territory in south-east Iberia (modern Spain and Portugal). When the Second Punic War broke out in 218 BC a Roman army landed in north-east Iberia. After a disastrous Roman setback in 210 BC Scipio took command and cleared the peninsula of Carthaginians in five years. He returned to Rome determined to carry the war to the Carthaginian homeland in North Africa. Appointed consul in 205 BC Scipio spent a year in Sicily training his army and accumulating supplies.
In 204 BC the Romans landed near the Carthaginian port of Utica with four legions. The Romans defeated two large Carthaginian scouting parties, besieged Utica and set up a fortified camp.

Bitka pri Utiki je potekala leta 203 pr. n. št. med rimsko vojsko pod poveljstvom Publija Kornelija Scipiona ter zavezniškima vojskama Kartagine in Numidije, ki sta jima poveljevala Hasdrubal Giskon oziroma Sifaks. Bitka je bila del druge punske vojne in se je končala s hudim porazom Kartagine.

Po porazu v prvi punski vojni (264–241 pr. n. št.) je Kartagina razširila svoje ozemlje na jugovzhodu Iberskega polotoka (današnja Španija in Portugalska). Ko je leta 218 pr. n. št. izbruhnila druga punska vojna, se je rimska vojska izkrcala na severovzhodu Iberskega polotoka. Po hudem rimskem porazu leta 210 pr. n. št. je poveljstvo prevzel Scipion in v petih letih pregnal Kartažane s polotoka. Vrnil se je v Rim, odločen, da vojno prenese v kartažansko domovino v severni Afriki. Leta 205 pr. n. št. so ga izvolili za konzula in leto dni je na Siciliji uril vojsko in zbiral zaloge.
Leta 204 pr. n. št. so se Rimljani s štirimi legijami izkrcali blizu kartažanskega pristanišča Utika. Premagali so dva velika kartažanska izvidniška oddelka, oblegali Utiko in postavili utrjen tabor.

events.label: Battle of the Great Plains
events.description: battle fought between Scipio Africanus of Rome and a combined Carthaginian and Numidian army late in the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of the Great Plains
story.description: 203 BC battle in the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The battle of the Great Plains was fought in 203 BC in modern Tunisia between a Roman army commanded by Publius Cornelius Scipio, and allied Carthaginian and Numidian armies commanded by Hasdrubal Gisco and Syphax respectively. The battle was part of the Second Punic War and resulted in a heavy defeat for Carthage.

In the wake of its defeat in the First Punic War (264–241 BC) Carthage expanded its territory in south-east Iberia (modern Spain and Portugal). When the Second Punic War broke out in 218 BC a Roman army landed in north-east Iberia. After a disastrous Roman setback in 211 BC, Scipio took command in 210 BC and cleared the peninsula of Carthaginians in five years. He returned to Rome determined to carry the war to the Carthaginian homeland in North Africa. Appointed consul in 205 BC Scipio spent a year in Sicily training his army and accumulating supplies. In 204 BC the Romans landed with four legions near the Carthaginian port of Utica and besieged it. The Carthaginians and their Numidian allies each set up their own camps about 11 kilometres (7 mi) from the Romans but close to each other. After several months of little activity Scipio launched a surprise night attack on both camps, overrunning them and setting fire to much of both. Carthaginian and Numidian casualties were heavy.

The Carthaginians reformed their army in an area known as the Great Plains, 120 kilometres (75 mi) from Utica. They were reinforced by 4,000 Iberian warriors to a total of about 30,000 men. Hearing of this, Scipio immediately marched most of his army to the scene. The size of his army is not known, but it was outnumbered by the Carthaginians. After several days of skirmishing, both armies committed to a pitched battle. Upon being charged by the Romans all of those Carthaginians who had been involved in the debacle at Utica turned and fled; morale had not recovered. Only the Iberians stood and fought. They were enveloped by the well-drilled Roman legions and wiped out.

Bitka na Velikih ravninah je potekala leta 203 pr. n. št. na ozemlju današnje Tunizije med rimsko vojsko pod poveljstvom Publija Kornelija Scipiona ter zavezniškima kartažansko in numidijsko vojsko, ki sta jima poveljevala Hasdrubal Giskon oziroma Sifaks. Bitka je bila del druge punske vojne in se je končala s hudim porazom Kartagine.

events.label: Po Valley Raid
events.description: culmination of a major diversion carried out by the Carthaginian commander Mago, son of Hamilcar Barca, at the end of the Second Punic war between Rome and Carthage in what is now northwestern Italy

story.title: Battle of Insubria
story.description: Battle in the Second Punic War
paragraphs: The Battle of Insubria in 203 BC was the culmination of a major war, carried out by the Carthaginian commander Mago, brother of Hannibal Barca, at the end of the Second Punic War between Rome and Carthage in what is now northwestern Italy. Mago had landed at Genoa, Liguria, two years before, in an effort to keep the Romans busy to the North and thus hamper indirectly their plans to invade Carthage's hinterland in Africa (modern Tunisia). He was quite successful in reigniting the unrest among various peoples (Ligurians, Gauls, Etruscans) against the Roman dominance. Rome was forced to concentrate large forces against him which finally resulted in a battle fought in the land of the Insubres (Lombardy). Mago suffered defeat and had to retreat. The strategy to divert the enemy's forces failed as the Roman general Publius Cornelius Scipio laid waste to Africa and wiped out the Carthaginian armies that were sent to destroy the invader. To counter Scipio, the Carthaginian government recalled Mago from Italy (along with his brother Hannibal, who had been in Bruttium until then). However, the remnants of the Carthaginian forces in Cisalpine Gaul continued to harass the Romans for several years after the end of the war.

events.label: Battle of Zama
events.description: final battle of the Second Punic War

story.title: Battle of Zama
story.description: Final battle of the Second Punic War (202 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Zama was fought in 202 BC in what is now Tunisia between a Roman army commanded by Scipio Africanus and a Carthaginian army commanded by Hannibal. The battle was part of the Second Punic War and resulted in such a severe defeat for the Carthaginians that they capitulated, while Hannibal was forced into exile. The Roman army of approximately 40,000 men was outnumbered by the Carthaginians who fielded either 40,000 or 50,000; the Romans were stronger in cavalry, but the Carthaginians had 80 war elephants.

At the outset of the Second Punic War, in 218 BC, a Carthaginian army led by Hannibal invaded mainland Italy, where it campaigned for the next 16 years. In 210 BC Scipio took command of the faltering Roman war effort in Iberia (modern Spain and Portugal) and cleared the peninsula of Carthaginians in five years. He returned to Rome and was appointed consul in 205 BC. The following year his army landed near the Carthaginian port of Utica. The Carthaginians and their Numidian allies were repeatedly beaten in battle and the Roman ally Masinissa became the leading Numidian ruler. Scipio and Carthage entered into peace negotiations, while Carthage recalled armies from Italy commanded by Hannibal and Mago Barca. The Roman Senate ratified a draft treaty, but when Hannibal arrived from Italy, Carthage repudiated it. Hannibal marched inland to confront the Romans and a battle quickly ensued.

events.label: Battle of the Aous
events.description: battle of the Second Macedonian War

story.title: Battle of the Aous (198 BC)
story.description: Battle of the Second Macedonian War
paragraphs: The Battle of the Aous was fought in 198 BC between the Roman Republic and the Kingdom of Macedon, in the area between modern Tepelenë and Këlcyrë in Albania. The Roman forces were led by Titus Quinctius Flamininus and the Macedonian ones were led by Philip V.

The Antigonid Macedonian army encamped behind a pass in an unassailable position. A local shepherd guided the Romans to a secret path that took them behind the Macedonian position. Flaminius led his troops through this secret path and attacked the Macedonians from the rear, rendering their position untenable and inflicting some 2,000 casualties. Philip's army retreated with the survivors, and the two commanders would meet again at Cynoscephalae the following year, where the Romans would triumph again and end the war.

Bitka ob Aoosu je potekala leta 198 pr. n. št. med Rimsko republiko in Makedonskim kraljestvom na območju med današnjima Tepeleno in Këlcyro v Albaniji. Rimske sile je vodil Tit Kvinkcij Flaminin, makedonske pa Filip V.

Antigonidska makedonska vojska se je utaborila za prelazom na nenapadljivem položaju. Krajevni pastir je Rimljane vodil po skrivni stezi za makedonski položaj. Flaminin je čete popeljal po tej stezi in Makedonce napadel od zadaj, zato njihovega položaja ni bilo več mogoče braniti; prizadejal jim je okoli 2000 izgub. Filipova vojska se je s preživelimi umaknila, poveljnika pa sta se naslednje leto znova srečala pri Kinoskefalah, kjer so Rimljani spet zmagali in končali vojno.

events.label: Battle of Cynoscephalae
events.description: battle of the Second Macedonian War

story.title: Battle of Cynoscephalae
story.description: 197 BC Roman victory in the Second Macedonian War
paragraphs: The Battle of Cynoscephalae (Greek: Μάχη τῶν Κυνὸς Κεφαλῶν) was an encounter battle fought in Thessaly in June 197 BC between the Roman-Aetolian army, led by Titus Quinctius Flamininus, and Antigonid Macedon, led by Philip V, during the Second Macedonian War. It was a decisive Roman victory and marked the end of the conflict.

Bitka pri Kinoskefalah (grško: Μάχη τῶν Κυνὸς Κεφαλῶν) je bila srečanjska bitka, ki je potekala junija 197 pr. n. št. v Tesaliji med rimsko-etolsko vojsko pod vodstvom Tita Kvinkcija Flaminina in antigonidsko Makedonijo pod vodstvom Filipa V. v drugi makedonski vojni. Bila je odločilna rimska zmaga in je končala spopad.

events.label: Battle of Thermopylae
events.description: 191 BCE battle of the Roman-Seleucid War

story.title: Battle of Thermopylae (191 BC)
story.description: Battle of the Roman–Seleucid War
paragraphs: The Battle of Thermopylae took place on 24 April 191 BC. It was fought as part of the Roman–Seleucid War, pitting forces of the Roman Republic led by the consul Manius Acilius Glabrio against a Seleucid-Aetolian army of Antiochus III the Great.

When the main bodies of the armies initially clashed at the Thermopylae pass, the Seleucids managed to hold their ground, repulsing multiple Roman assaults. However, a small Roman force under Marcus Porcius Cato managed to outflank the Seleucids from the hillside after surprising the Aetolian garrison of Fort Callidromus. The Seleucids panicked and broke ranks, leading to the destruction of their force. Antiochus managed to escape the battlefield with his cavalry, departing mainland Greece soon afterwards.

Bitka pri Termopilah je potekala 24. aprila 191 pr. n. št. v rimsko-selevkidski vojni; sile Rimske republike pod vodstvom konzula Manija Acilija Glabriona so se v njej spopadle s selevkidsko-etolsko vojsko Antioha III. Velikega.

Ko sta se glavnini vojsk najprej spopadli na prelazu Termopile, so se Selevkidi obdržali in odbili več rimskih napadov. Toda majhen rimski oddelek pod vodstvom Marka Porcija Katona je presenetil etolsko posadko utrdbe Kalidromos in Selevkide obšel s pobočja. Selevkide je zajela panika, njihova bojna vrsta je razpadla in vojska je bila uničena. Antiohu je s konjenico uspelo pobegniti z bojišča in kmalu zatem je zapustil grško celino.

events.label: Battle of Magnesia
events.description: battle

story.title: Battle of Magnesia
story.description: 190/89 BCE battle in which Rome and Pergamon defeated the Seleucids
paragraphs: The Battle of Magnesia took place in either December 190 or January 189 BC. It was fought as part of the Roman–Seleucid War, pitting forces of the Roman Republic led by the consul Lucius Cornelius Scipio Asiaticus and the allied Kingdom of Pergamon under Eumenes II against a Seleucid army of Antiochus III the Great. The two armies initially camped northeast of Magnesia ad Sipylum in Asia Minor (modern-day Manisa, Turkey), attempting to provoke each other into a battle on favorable terrain for several days.

When the battle finally began, Eumenes managed to throw the Seleucid left flank into disarray. While Antiochus' cavalry overpowered his adversaries on the right flank of the battlefield, his army's center collapsed before he could reinforce it. Modern estimates give 10,000 dead for the Seleucids and 5,000 killed for the Romans. The battle resulted in a decisive Roman-Pergamene victory, which led to the Treaty of Apamea that ended Seleucid domination in Asia Minor.

Bitka pri Magneziji je potekala decembra 190 ali januarja 189 pr. n. št. Bila je del rimsko-selevkidske vojne: sile Rimske republike pod vodstvom konzula Lucija Kornelija Scipiona Azijskega in zavezniškega Kraljestva Pergamon pod Evmenom II. so se spopadle s selevkidsko vojsko Antioha III. Velikega. Vojski sta se sprva utaborili severovzhodno od Magnezije ob Sipilu v Mali Aziji (današnja Manisa v Turčiji) in več dni skušali druga drugo izzvati v bitko na ugodnem terenu.

Ko se je bitka nazadnje začela, je Evmen uspel zmesti levo krilo Selevkidov. Medtem ko je Antiohova konjenica na desnem krilu bojišča premagovala nasprotnike, je središče njegove vojske razpadlo, preden ga je lahko okrepil. Po sodobnih ocenah je padlo 10.000 Selevkidov in 5000 Rimljanov. Bitka se je končala z odločilno rimsko-pergamsko zmago, ki je pripeljala do mira v Apameji, s katerim je bilo konec selevkidske prevlade v Mali Aziji.

events.label: Battle of Myonessus
events.description: battle

story.title: Battle of Myonessus
story.description: Naval battle where Rome and Rhodes defeat the Seleucids
paragraphs: The Battle of Myonessus took place in September 190 BC. It was fought as part of the Roman–Seleucid War, pitting the fleets of the Roman Republic led by Admiral Lucius Aemilius Regillus and its Rhodian allies under Eudamus against a Seleucid fleet of Polyxenidas.

Polyxenidas attacked his adversaries as they were putting to sea between Myonessus and the Corycus peninsula. The Roman–Rhodian fleet withstood the first assault, managing to assume battle formation. Eudamus then led the Rhodian squadron to the right flank of the Romans, thwarting a Seleucid attempt at encirclement and overpowering the Seleucid seaward wing. Polyxenidas withdrew, having lost half of his fleet. The battle cemented Roman control over the Aegean Sea, enabling them to launch an invasion of Seleucid Asia Minor.

Bitka pri Mionesu je potekala septembra 190 pr. n. št. Bila je del rimsko-selevkidske vojne: ladjevje Rimske republike pod vodstvom admirala Lucija Emilija Regila in njegovi rodoški zavezniki pod Evdamom so se spopadli s selevkidskim ladjevjem Poliksenidasa.

Poliksenidas je nasprotnike napadel, ko so izplovljali med Mionesom in polotokom Korikos. Rimsko-rodoško ladjevje je prvi napad zdržalo in se postavilo v bojni red. Evdam je nato rodoško eskadro povedel na desno krilo Rimljanov, preprečil selevkidski poskus obkolitve in premagal selevkidsko krilo na morski strani. Poliksenidas se je umaknil, potem ko je izgubil polovico ladjevja. Bitka je Rimljanom utrdila nadzor nad Egejskim morjem in jim omogočila vdor v selevkidsko Malo Azijo.

events.label: Battle of the Eurymedon
events.description: naval battle where Rhodes defeat the Seleucids

story.title: Battle of the Eurymedon (190 BC)
story.description: Naval battle where Rhodes defeat the Seleucids
paragraphs: The Battle of the Eurymedon, also known as the Battle of Side took place in August 190 BC. It was fought as part of the Roman–Seleucid War, pitting the fleets of Rhodes under admiral Eudamus against a Seleucid fleet of Hannibal.

The battle took place off Side, when Hannibal attacked the Rhodian fleet docked in the mouth of Eurymedon River. After overcoming some initial confusion, the Rhodians executed the diekplous maneuver against the Seleucid seaward wing. Half of the Seleucid ships were heavily damaged, forcing them to withdraw. While Hannibal managed to preserve most of his fleet, he was unable to reinforce the rest of the Seleucid navy in Ephesus which left it isolated and vulnerable. This allowed the Romans to proceed with their invasion of Seleucid Asia Minor.

Bitka pri Evrimedontu, znana tudi kot bitka pri Sidi, je potekala avgusta 190 pr. n. št. Bila je del rimsko-selevkidske vojne: rodoško ladjevje pod admiralom Evdamom se je spopadlo s selevkidskim ladjevjem Hanibala.

Bitka je potekala pred Sido, ko je Hanibal napadel rodoško ladjevje, zasidrano v ustju reke Evrimedont. Ko so Rodošani premagali začetno zmedo, so proti selevkidskemu krilu na morski strani izvedli manever diekplous. Polovica selevkidskih ladij je bila hudo poškodovana, zato so se morale umakniti. Hanibal je sicer ohranil večji del ladjevja, ni pa mogel okrepiti preostale selevkidske mornarice v Efezu, ki je tako ostala osamljena in ranljiva. To je Rimljanom omogočilo, da so nadaljevali vdor v selevkidsko Malo Azijo.

events.label: Treaty of Apamea
events.description: Hellenistic peace treaty (188 BCE)

story.title: Treaty of Apamea
story.description: 188 BC peace treaty between the Roman Republic and Seleucid Empire
paragraphs: The Treaty of Apamea was a peace treaty conducted in 188 BC between the Roman Republic and Antiochus III, ruler of the Seleucid Empire. It ended the Roman–Seleucid War. The treaty took place after Roman victories at the Battle of Thermopylae (in 191 BC), the Battle of Magnesia (in 190 BC), and after Roman and Rhodian naval victories over the Seleucid navy.

editorial.why: Ended the Roman–Seleucid War; Wikidata links it to no war.
editorial.quote: between the Roman Republic and Antiochus III

events.label: Battle of Callinicus
events.description: battle of the Third Macedonian War

story.title: Battle of Callinicus
story.description: 171 BCE battle of the Third Macedonian War
paragraphs: The Battle of Callinicus (Greek: μάχη του Καλλίνικου) was fought in 171 BC between Macedonia and the Roman Republic near a hill called Callinicus, close to the Roman camp at Tripolis Larisaia, five kilometres north of Larissa, the capital of Thessaly. It was fought during the first year of the Third Macedonian War (171-168 BC). The Macedonians were led by their king, Perseus of Macedon, while the Roman force was led by the consul Publius Licinius Crassus. The Macedonians were supported by Cotys IV, the king of the Odrysian kingdom (the largest state in Thrace) and his forces, Cretan mercenaries, and auxiliaries of mixed nationalities. The Romans had their Italian allies with them and were supported by soldiers provided by Eumenes II of Pergamon, as well as a force of Thessalian cavalry and Greek allies. The battle saw the deployment of troops with cavalry intermixed with light infantry. Although the battle was actually inconclusive because Perseus withdrew before it came to a conclusion, it was considered a Macedonian victory because the Romans suffered heavy casualties.

Bitka pri Kaliniku (grško: μάχη του Καλλίνικου) je potekala leta 171 pr. n. št. med Makedonijo in Rimsko republiko blizu griča Kalinik, v bližini rimskega tabora v Tripolisu Larisaji, pet kilometrov severno od Larise, glavnega mesta Tesalije. Spopad se je zgodil v prvem letu tretje makedonske vojne (171–168 pr. n. št.). Makedonce je vodil njihov kralj Perzej Makedonski, rimske sile pa konzul Publij Licinij Kras. Makedonce so podpirali Kotis IV., kralj Odriškega kraljestva (največje države v Trakiji), s svojimi silami, kretski najemniki in pomožne čete mešanih narodnosti. Rimljani so imeli s seboj italske zaveznike, podpirali pa so jih vojaki, ki jih je poslal Evmen II. Pergamski, ter oddelek tesalske konjenice in grški zavezniki. V bitki so konjenico pomešali z lahko pehoto. Bitka se dejansko ni odločila, ker se je Perzej umaknil, preden se je končala, vendar so jo šteli za makedonsko zmago, saj so Rimljani utrpeli hude izgube.

events.label: Battle of Pydna
events.description: battle of the Third Macedonian War

story.title: Battle of Pydna
story.description: Battle of the Third Macedonian War in 168 BC
paragraphs: The Battle of Pydna took place in 168 BC between Rome and Macedon during the Third Macedonian War. The battle saw the further ascendancy of Rome in the Hellenistic world and the end of the Antigonid line of kings, whose power traced back to Alexander the Great's Diadochi Antigonus Monophthalmus. The battle is also considered to be a victory of the Roman legion's manipular system's flexibility over the Antigonid Macedonian phalanx's rigidity.

Bitka pri Pidni je potekala leta 168 pr. n. št. med Rimom in Makedonijo v tretji makedonski vojni. Z njo se je vpliv Rima v helenističnem svetu še povečal, končala pa se je tudi vladarska rodbina Antigonidov, katere moč je izhajala iz Aleksandrovega diadoha Antigona Monoftalma. Bitka velja tudi za zmago prožnega manipularnega sistema rimske legije nad togo antigonidsko makedonsko falango.

events.label: Siege of Carthage
events.description: main engagement of the Third Punic War in which the Roman Republic besieged the Punic city of Carthage in c. 149–146 BCE

story.title: Siege of Carthage (Third Punic War)
story.description: Carthage-Rome engagement, 149–146 BCE
paragraphs: The siege of Carthage was the main engagement of the Third Punic War fought between Carthage and Rome. It consisted of the nearly three-year siege of the Carthaginian capital, Carthage (a little northeast of Tunis). In 149 BC, a large Roman army landed at Utica in North Africa. The Carthaginians hoped to appease the Romans, but despite the Carthaginians surrendering all of their weapons, the Romans pressed on to besiege the city. The Roman campaign suffered repeated setbacks through 149 BC, only alleviated by Scipio Aemilianus, a middle-ranking officer, distinguishing himself several times. A new Roman commander took over in 148 BC, and fared equally badly. At the annual election of Roman magistrates in early 147 BC, the public support for Scipio was so great that the usual age restrictions were lifted to allow him to be appointed commander in Africa.

Scipio's term began with two Carthaginian successes, but he tightened the siege and commenced a construction of a large mole to prevent supplies from getting into Carthage via blockade runners. The Carthaginians had partially rebuilt their fleet and it sortied, to the Romans' surprise; after an indecisive engagement the Carthaginians mismanaged their withdrawal and lost many ships. The Romans then built a large brick structure in the harbour area, which dominated the city wall. In early 146 BC the Romans launched their final assault, and over one week systematically destroyed the city and killed its inhabitants; only on the last day did they take prisoners – 50,000, who were sold into slavery. The formerly Carthaginian territories became the Roman province of Africa, with Utica as its capital. It was a century before the site of Carthage was rebuilt as a Roman city.

events.label: Battle of Pydna
events.description: battle of the Fourth Macedonian War

story.title: Battle of Pydna (148 BC)
story.description: Battle of the Fourth Macedonian War
paragraphs: The Battle of Pydna was fought in 148 BC between Rome and the forces of the Macedonian leader Andriscus. The Roman force was led by Quintus Caecilius Metellus, and was victorious. The battle played an important role in deciding the outcome of the Fourth Macedonian War, and saw the annihilation of the last military-political force of Macedon.

The war had begun when the pretender Andriscus defeated Rome's clients in Macedon and crowned himself king, defeating a Roman force sent to stop him and invading parts of Greece. The senate then sent Quintus Caecilius Metellus with another, larger army to stop the pretender; the Roman commander chose to undertake both a land and sea offensive, forcing Andriscus to take a defensive position near Pydna, where Metellus engaged and soundly defeated him.

The battle decided the outcome of the war; Andriscus was forced to flee Macedon, and was pursued and captured by the Romans before he could raise a strong army. Rome now took direct control of Macedon, making it a Roman province.

Bitka pri Pidni je potekala leta 148 pr. n. št. med Rimom in silami makedonskega voditelja Andriska. Rimske sile pod vodstvom Kvinta Cecilija Metela so zmagale. Bitka je odločilno vplivala na izid četrte makedonske vojne, v njej pa je bila uničena zadnja vojaško-politična sila Makedonije.

Vojna se je začela, ko je pretendent Andrisk premagal rimske varovance v Makedoniji in se okronal za kralja, nato pa porazil rimsko vojsko, poslano, da bi ga ustavila, in vdrl v dele Grčije. Senat je nato proti pretendentu poslal Kvinta Cecilija Metela z drugo, večjo vojsko; rimski poveljnik se je odločil za ofenzivo po kopnem in morju ter Andriska prisilil v obrambni položaj blizu Pidne, kjer ga je napadel in hudo porazil.

Bitka je odločila izid vojne: Andrisk je moral zbežati iz Makedonije, Rimljani pa so ga zasledovali in ujeli, preden je lahko zbral močno vojsko. Rim je nato Makedonijo prevzel pod neposredno oblast in jo spremenil v rimsko provinco.

events.label: Battle of Corinth
events.description: 146 BCE battle between the Roman Republic and Corinth and its allies

story.title: Battle of Corinth (146 BC)
story.description: Battle between the Roman Republic and Corinth and its allies in 146 BC
paragraphs: The Battle of Corinth of 146 BC, also known as the Battle of Leucapetra or the Battle of Lefkopetra, was a decisive engagement fought between the Roman Republic and the Greek city-state of Corinth and its allies in the Achaean League. The battle marked the end of the Achaean War and the beginning of the period of Roman domination in Greek history, and is also notable for the complete destruction of Corinth by the Romans in its aftermath.

The Romans had moved swiftly since the war's beginning a few weeks earlier; they had destroyed the main Achaean force at Scarpheia, conquered Boeotia and then proceeded to Corinth itself. Despite the Roman successes, the Achaeans refused to surrender and gathered a final army for the defense of the League's capital of Corinth, where they engaged the Romans in battle. In a few hours of fighting, the Achaeans were soundly routed, with their troops killed, captured, or put to flight. After a few days' waiting, the Romans entered the city, and, on the orders of Mummius, set it on fire, killed all the men and enslaved all the women and children, after which the rest of Greece was subjugated by Rome.

Bitka pri Korintu leta 146 pr. n. št., znana tudi kot bitka pri Levkopetri ali Lefkopetri, je bila odločilen spopad med Rimsko republiko ter grško mestno državo Korint in njenimi zaveznicami v Ahajski zvezi. Z njo se je končala ahajska vojna in začelo obdobje rimske prevlade v grški zgodovini, znana pa je tudi po tem, da so Rimljani Korint po njej popolnoma porušili.

events.label: Battle of Noreia
events.description: 113 BCE battle of the Cimbrian War

story.title: Battle of Noreia
story.description: Battle during the Cimbrian War (113 BCE)
paragraphs: The Battle of Noreia, in 113 BC, was the opening battle of the Cimbrian War fought between the Roman Republic and the migrating Proto-Germanic tribes, the Cimbri and the Teutons. It ended in defeat, and near disaster, for the Romans.

Bitka pri Noreji leta 113 pr. n. št. je bila uvodna bitka kimbrske vojne med rimsko republiko in selečima se protogermanskima plemenoma Kimbrov in Tevtonov. Končala se je z rimskim porazom, ki je bil skoraj katastrofa.

events.label: Battle of Burdigala
events.description: battle

story.title: Battle of Burdigala
story.description: Battle during the Cimbrian War (107 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Burdigala (the Roman name for Bordeaux) took place during the Cimbrian War in 107 BC. The battle was fought between a combined Celtic-Germanic army including the Helvetian Tigurini under the command of Divico, and the forces of the Roman Republic under the command of Lucius Cassius Longinus, Lucius Caesoninus, and Gaius Popillius Laenas. Longinus and Caesoninus were killed in the fighting and the battle resulted in a victory for the Celtic-Germanic tribes.

Bitka pri Burdigali (rimsko ime za Bordeaux) je potekala med kimbrsko vojno leta 107 pr. n. št. V njej sta se spopadli združena keltsko-germanska vojska, v kateri so bili tudi helvetski Tigurini pod poveljstvom Divikona, in vojska rimske republike pod poveljstvom Lucija Kasija Longina, Lucija Cezonina in Gaja Popilija Laenata. Longin in Cezonin sta v bojih padla, bitka pa se je končala z zmago keltsko-germanskih plemen.

events.label: Battle of Arausio
events.description: battle between the ancient Roman Republic and several German tribes

story.title: Battle of Arausio
story.description: Battle during the Cimbrian War (105 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Arausio took place on 6 October 105 BC, at a site between the town of Arausio, now Orange, Vaucluse, and the Rhône river, when two Roman armies, commanded by proconsul Quintus Servilius Caepio and consul Gnaeus Mallius Maximus, suffered a major defeat at the hands of the Cimbri and Teuton migratory tribes who were led by Boiorix and Teutobod respectively.

Differences between the Roman commanders prevented regular coordination between their armies, resulting in their annihilation by the united Cimbrian-Teutonic force. Roman losses are thought to have been as high as 80,000 legionaries and another 40,000 auxiliary troops, with total losses numbering up to 120,000 soldiers, the entirety of both armies. In terms of losses, this battle is regarded as the worst defeat in the history of ancient Rome, surpassing the Battle of Cannae. The battle resulted in the Roman military being restructured under Gaius Marius through his Marian reforms, which significantly changed the organisation and recruitment of Roman legions. These changes would remain principally intact for centuries. However, some historians have questioned the implementation of sudden reforms under Marius.

Bitka pri Arausiu je potekala 6. oktobra 105 pr. n. št. med mestom Arausio (danes Orange v departmaju Vaucluse) in reko Rono. Dve rimski vojski pod poveljstvom prokonzula Kvinta Servilija Cepiona in konzula Gneja Malija Maksima sta tam doživeli hud poraz proti selečima se plemenoma Kimbrov in Tevtonov, ki sta ju vodila Bojoriks oziroma Tevtobod.

events.label: Battle of Aquae Sextiae
events.description: 102 BCE battle of the Cimbrian War

story.title: Battle of Aquae Sextiae
story.description: Battle during the Cimbrian War (102 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Aquae Sextiae (Aix-en-Provence) took place in 102 BC. After a series of Roman defeats at the Battle of Noreia, the Battle of Burdigala, and most notably at the Battle of Arausio, the Romans under Gaius Marius finally defeated the Teutons and Ambrones as they attempted to advance through the Alps into Italy. Local lore associates the name of the mountain, Mont St. Victoire, with the Roman victory at the battle of Aquae Sextiae, but Frédéric Mistral and other scholars have debunked this theory.

Bitka pri Aquae Sextiae (Aix-en-Provence) je potekala leta 102 pr. n. št. Po vrsti rimskih porazov v bitki pri Noreji, bitki pri Burdigali in predvsem v bitki pri Arausiu so Rimljani pod vodstvom Gaja Marija nazadnje premagali Tevtone in Ambrone, ko so ti skušali prek Alp prodreti v Italijo. Lokalno izročilo ime gore Mont Sainte-Victoire povezuje z rimsko zmago v bitki pri Aquae Sextiae, a so Frédéric Mistral in drugi raziskovalci to razlago ovrgli.

events.label: Battle of Vercellae
events.description: Final battle of the Cimbrian war

story.title: Battle of Vercellae
story.description: Battle during the Cimbrian War (101 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Vercellae or Battle of the Raudine Plain was fought on 30 July 101 BC on a plain near Vercellae in Gallia Cisalpina, modern-day Northern Italy. A Celtic-Germanic confederation under the command of the Cimbric king Boiorix was defeated by a Roman army under the joint command of the consul Gaius Marius and the proconsul Quintus Lutatius Catulus. The battle marked the end of the Cimbrian War.

Bitka pri Vercellae ali bitka na Raudijski ravnini je potekala 30. julija 101 pr. n. št. na ravnini blizu Vercellae v Cisalpinski Galiji, današnji severni Italiji. Keltsko-germansko zvezo pod poveljstvom kimbrskega kralja Boiorixa je premagala rimska vojska pod skupnim poveljstvom konzula Gaja Marija in prokonzula Kvinta Lutacija Katula. Z bitko se je končala kimbrska vojna.

events.label: Battle of Asculum
events.description: 88 BCE battle

story.title: Siege of Asculum (90–89 BC)
story.description: Roman battle of the Social War
paragraphs: The Battle of Asculum was fought in 89 BC during the Social War between Rome and its former Italian allies. The Romans were led by Gnaeus Pompeius Strabo, and were victorious over the rebels. Many scholars consider this battle to have been the turning point in the war.

Bitka pri Askulu je potekala leta 89 pr. n. št. v zavezniški vojni med Rimom in njegovimi nekdanjimi italijskimi zavezniki. Rimljane je vodil Gnej Pompej Strabon, ki je nad uporniki zmagal. Mnogi raziskovalci menijo, da je bila ta bitka prelomnica vojne.

events.label: Battle of Chaeronea
events.description: battle in 86 BCE

story.title: Battle of Chaeronea (86 BC)
story.description: Victory of Sulla over Archelaus of Pontus
paragraphs: The Battle of Chaeronea was fought by the Roman forces of Lucius Cornelius Sulla and Mithridates' general, Archelaus, near Chaeronea, in Boeotia, in 86 BC during the First Mithridatic War. The battle ended with a complete rout of the Pontic army and a decisive victory for the Romans.

Bitka pri Heroneji je potekala leta 86 pr. n. št. v prvi mitridatski vojni blizu Heroneje v Beotiji med rimskimi silami Lucija Kornelija Sule in Mitridatovim vojskovodjo Arhelajem. Končala se je s popolnim porazom pontske vojske in odločilno zmago Rimljanov.

events.label: Battle of Orchomenus
events.description: 85 BCE battle

story.title: Battle of Orchomenus
story.description: Battle between the Roman Republic and the Kingdom of Pontus
paragraphs: The Battle of Orchomenus was fought in autumn 86 BC between Rome and the forces of Mithridates VI of Pontus. The Roman army was led by Lucius Cornelius Sulla, while Mithridates' army was led by Archelaus. The Roman force was victorious, and Archelaus later defected to Rome. The battle ended the Mithridatic invasion of Europe. Information on the battle is included in Plutarch's Life of Sulla, chapters 20–21.

Bitka pri Orhomenu je potekala jeseni leta 86 pr. n. št. med Rimom in silami Mitridata VI. Pontskega. Rimsko vojsko je vodil Lucij Kornelij Sula, Mitridatovo pa Arhelaj. Zmagali so Rimljani, Arhelaj pa je pozneje prestopil na rimsko stran. Bitka je končala Mitridatov vdor v Evropo. Podatki o njej so v Plutarhovem Sulovem življenjepisu, v poglavjih 20–21.

events.label: Treaty of Dardanos
events.description: 85 BC treaty between Rome and Pontus

story.title: Treaty of Dardanos
story.description: 85 BC treaty between Sulla and Mithridates of Pontus
paragraphs: The Treaty of Dardanos (85 BC) was a treaty between Rome and Pontus signed between Lucius Cornelius Sulla of Rome and King Mithridates VI of Pontus. It ended the First Mithridatic War.
Mir v Dardanu (85 pr. n. št.) je bil pogodba med Rimom in Pontom, ki sta jo podpisala Rimljan Lucij Kornelij Sula in pontski kralj Mitridat VI. Z njo se je končala prva mitridatska vojna.

editorial.why: Ended the First Mithridatic War; Wikidata links it to no war.

events.label: Battle of the Colline Gate
events.description: 82 BCE battle

story.title: Battle of the Colline Gate
story.description: Battle during Sulla's civil war, 82 BC
paragraphs: The Battle of the Colline Gate, fought on 1 November 82 BC, was the decisive battle of the civil war between Lucius Cornelius Sulla and the Marians, Samnites and Lucanians. Sulla won the battle at the northeastern end of Rome, near the Colline Gate, and secured control of Italy. Appian is the only source who provides details about the battle.
The next day Sulla ordered the slaughter of the Marian leaders and Samnite prisoners in the Villa Publica. On 3 November, he started the proscription of his enemies.

Bitka pri Kolinskih vratih, ki je potekala 1. novembra 82 pr. n. št., je bila odločilna bitka državljanske vojne med Lucijem Kornelijem Sulo ter Marijevci, Samniti in Lukanci. Sula je bitko dobil na severovzhodnem koncu Rima, blizu Kolinskih vrat, in si zagotovil nadzor nad Italijo. Podrobnosti o bitki navaja samo Apijan.
Naslednji dan je Sula ukazal pobiti marijevske voditelje in samnitske ujetnike v Villi Publici. 3. novembra je začel s proskripcijo svojih sovražnikov.

events.label: Battle of the Silarius River
events.description: last battle of the Roman Servile War, 71 BC

story.title: Battle of the Silarius River
story.description: Last battle of the Roman Servile War, 71 BC
paragraphs: The Battle of the Silarius River was the final, decisive action of the Third Servile War, the last of the Roman Servile Wars. It occurred near the mouth of modern Sele River, southern Campania, southern Italy.
Bitka ob reki Silarius je bila zadnji, odločilni spopad tretje suženjske vojne, zadnje od rimskih suženjskih vojn. Potekala je blizu izliva današnje reke Sele v južni Kampaniji v južni Italiji.

events.label: Battle of Tigranocerta
events.description: battle fought in 69 BCE

story.title: Battle of Tigranocerta
story.description: 69 BC battle between Rome and Armenia
paragraphs: The Battle of Tigranocerta (Armenian: Տիգրանակերտի ճակատամարտ, Tigranakerti tchakatamart) was fought on 6 October 69 BC between the forces of the Roman Republic and the army of the Kingdom of Armenia led by King Tigranes the Great. The Roman force, led by Consul Lucius Licinius Lucullus, defeated Tigranes, and as a result, captured Tigranes' capital city of Tigranocerta.

The battle arose from the Third Mithridatic War being fought between the Roman Republic and Mithridates VI of Pontus, whose daughter Cleopatra was married to Tigranes. Mithridates fled to seek shelter with his son-in-law, and Rome invaded the Kingdom of Armenia. Having laid siege to Tigranocerta, the Roman forces fell back behind a nearby river when the large Armenian army approached. Feigning retreat, the Romans crossed at a ford and fell on the right flank of the Armenian army. After the Romans defeated the Armenian cataphracts, the balance of Tigranes' army, which was mostly made up of raw levies and peasant troops from his extensive empire, panicked and fled, and the Romans remained in charge of the field.

Bitka pri Tigranokerti (armensko: Տիգրանակերտի ճակատամարտ, Tigranakerti tchakatamart) je potekala 6. oktobra 69 pr. n. št. med silami Rimske republike in vojsko Kraljevine Armenije pod vodstvom kralja Tigrana Velikega. Rimska vojska pod vodstvom konzula Lucija Licinija Lukula je premagala Tigrana in nato zavzela njegovo prestolnico Tigranokerto.

Do bitke je prišlo v tretji mitridatski vojni, ki sta jo bojevala Rimska republika in pontski kralj Mitridat VI., čigar hči Kleopatra je bila Tigranova žena. Mitridat se je zatekel k zetu, Rim pa je vdrl v Kraljevino Armenijo. Rimske sile so oblegale Tigranokerto, ko pa se je približala velika armenska vojska, so se umaknile za bližnjo reko. Rimljani so se navidezno umaknili, prečkali reko pri gazu in napadli desno krilo armenske vojske. Ko so Rimljani premagali armenske katafrakte, se je preostanek Tigranove vojske, sestavljen večinoma iz neizurjenih nabornikov in kmečkih čet iz njegovega obsežnega imperija, v paniki razbežal, bojišče pa je ostalo v rimskih rokah.

events.label: Battle of Artaxata
events.description: battle between the Roman Republic and the Kingdom of Armenia

story.title: Battle of Artaxata
story.description: 68 BC battle between Romans and Armenians
paragraphs: The Battle of Artaxata was fought near the Arsanias River in 68 BC between an army of the Roman Republic and the army of the Kingdom of Armenia. The Romans were led by proconsul Lucius Licinius Lucullus, while the Armenians were led by Tigranes II of Armenia, who was sheltering Mithridates VI of Pontus, his father-in-law and refugee King of Pontus. The battle was part of the Third Mithridatic War and ended in a Roman victory.

Bitka pri Artaksati je potekala leta 68 pr. n. št. blizu reke Arsanias med vojsko Rimske republike in vojsko Kraljevine Armenije. Rimljane je vodil prokonzul Lucij Licinij Lukul, Armence pa armenski kralj Tigran II., ki je dajal zatočišče svojemu tastu, pontskemu kralju Mitridatu VI., ki je pobegnil iz Ponta. Bitka je bila del tretje mitridatske vojne in se je končala z rimsko zmago.

events.label: Siege of Jerusalem
events.description: 63 BCE siege, part of Pompey the Great's campaigns in the East

story.title: Siege of Jerusalem (63 BC)
story.description: Part of Pompey the Great's campaigns in the East
paragraphs: The siege of Jerusalem in 63 BC occurred during the campaigns of Roman general Pompey the Great in the East, shortly after his successful conclusion of the Third Mithridatic War. Pompey had been asked to intervene in a dispute over succession to the Hasmonean throne, which turned into a war between Hyrcanus II and Aristobulus II. His conquest of Jerusalem spelled the end of an independent Jewish state, and thus the incorporation of Judea as a client kingdom of the Roman Republic and later as a province of the Roman Empire.

Obleganje Jeruzalema leta 63 pr. n. št. je potekalo med pohodi rimskega vojskovodje Pompeja Velikega na vzhodu, kmalu potem, ko je uspešno končal tretjo mitridatsko vojno. Pompeja so prosili, naj posreduje v sporu o nasledstvu hasmonejskega prestola, ki je prerasel v vojno med Hirkanom II. in Aristobulom II. Z njegovim zavzetjem Jeruzalema je bilo konec samostojne judovske države: Judeja je postala vazalno kraljestvo Rimske republike in pozneje provinca Rimskega cesarstva.

events.label: Battle of Bibracte
events.description: battle in 58 BC

story.title: Battle of Bibracte
story.description: Helvetii v. Rome, Gallic Wars, 58 BC
paragraphs: The Battle of Bibracte was fought between a Gallic confederation centred around the Helvetii and a Roman army under the command of Gaius Julius Caesar. It was the first major battle of the Gallic Wars.
Bitka pri Bibractu je bila spopad med galsko zvezo s središčem okoli Helvečanov in rimsko vojsko pod poveljstvom Gaja Julija Cezarja. Bila je prva velika bitka galskih vojn.

events.label: Battle of Vosges
events.description: battle between the Germanic tribe of the Suebi under the leadership of Ariovistus against six Roman legions under the command of Gaius Julius Caesar in 58 BCE

story.title: Battle of Vosges (58 BC)
story.description: Battle during Gallic Wars (58 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of Vosges, also referred to as the Battle of Vesontio, was fought on September 14, 58 BC between a coalition of Germanic tribes, under the leadership of Ariovistus, and a Roman army supported by Gallic allies under the overall command of Gaius Julius Caesar. This encounter is the second major battle of the Gallic Wars.

During the late 60s and early 50s BC several Germanic tribes had crossed the Rhine, seeking a home in Gaul. Feeling threatened, a number of Gallic tribes, allied to the Roman Republic, had petitioned the Romans to come to their aid. Gaius Julius Caesar, who was governor of the Roman province of Gallia Transalpina and who had just finished his campaign against the Helvetii, decided to continue his military campaign in Gaul and marched his army towards the migrating Germans.

Prior to the battle, Caesar and Ariovistus held a parley. Ariovistus' cavalry cast stones and weapons at the Roman cavalry. Caesar broke off negotiations and instructed his men not to retaliate to prevent the Suebi from claiming that they were induced into a trap by their accepting an opportunity to talk. The following battle resulted in a Roman victory, which secured the eastern borderlands of Gaul, and allowed the temporary construction of Caesar's Rhine bridges for a tactical punitive assault staged in western Germania.

events.label: Battle of the Arar
events.description: battle between the migrating tribes of the Helvetii, and four Roman legions (Legions VII, VIII, IX, and X) under the command of Gaius Julius Caesar

story.title: Battle of the Arar
story.description: Part of the Gallic War (58 BCE)
paragraphs: The Battle of the Arar was fought between the migrating tribes of the Helvetii and six Roman legions under the command of Gaius Julius Caesar in 58 BC. It was the first major battle of the Gallic Wars and ended in a tactical victory for the outnumbered Roman army.

Bitka na reki Arar je bila spopad med selečimi se plemeni Helvečanov in šestimi rimskimi legijami pod poveljstvom Gaja Julija Cezarja leta 58 pr. n. št. Bila je prva velika bitka galskih vojn in se je končala s taktično zmago številčno šibkejše rimske vojske.

events.label: Battle of Octodurus
events.description: battle of the Gallic War

story.title: Battle of Octodurus
story.description: Battle in the winter of 57–56 BCE
paragraphs: The battle of Octodurus took place in the winter of 57–56 BC in the Gallic town of Octodurus in what is now Martigny, Valais, Switzerland. The battle resulted from a Roman attempt to open the Great St. Bernard Pass over the Alps. It was a Roman victory, but the ferocity of the fighting ended with the Roman legion moving back out of the Alps.

Bitka v Oktoduru je potekala pozimi 57–56 pr. n. št. v galskem mestu Oktodur na območju današnjega Martignyja v kantonu Valais v Švici. Do nje je prišlo zaradi rimskega poskusa, da bi odprli prelaz Veliki Sveti Bernard čez Alpe. Bila je rimska zmaga, a zaradi srditosti bojev se je rimska legija umaknila iz Alp.

events.label: Battle of the Axona
events.description: battle between the Roman army of Gaius Julius Caesar and the Belgae

story.title: Battle of the Axona
story.description: Battle between the Roman army of Gaius Julius Caesar and the Belgae
paragraphs: The Battle of the Axona was fought in 57 BC, between the Roman army of Gaius Julius Caesar and the Belgae. The Belgae, led by King Galba of the Suessiones, attacked, only to be repelled by Caesar. Fearing an ambush, the Romans delayed their pursuit. Caesar's Commentarii de Bello Gallico describes this battle at 2.7 - 2.11.

Bitka na Axoni je potekala leta 57 pr. n. št. med rimsko vojsko Gaja Julija Cezarja in Belgi. Belgi pod vodstvom kralja Suesionov Galbe so napadli, a jih je Cezar odbil. Rimljani so zasledovanje odložili, ker so se bali zasede. Cezar bitko opisuje v Zapiskih o galski vojni (Commentarii de Bello Gallico), 2.7–2.11.

events.label: Battle of the Sabis
events.description: battle between the legions of the Roman Republic and an association of Belgic tribes, principally the Nervii

story.title: Battle of the Sabis
story.description: Battle between Caesar and the Belgae tribes, part of Caesar's Gallic Wars (57 BC)
paragraphs: The Battle of the Sabis also (arguably erroneously) known as the Battle of the Sambre or the Battle against the Nervians (or Nervii) was fought in 57 BC near modern Saulzoir in Northern France. At the River Sabis a Roman army under the command of Gaius Julius Caesar fought an association of Belgae tribes, principally the Nervii. Caesar was surprised and nearly defeated by a Belgae surprise attack. According to Caesar's commentaries, a combination of determined defence, skilled generalship, and the timely arrival of reinforcements allowed the Romans to turn the Belgae ambush into a Roman victory. Few primary sources describe the battle in detail, with most information coming from Caesar's own report on the battle from his book, Commentarii de Bello Gallico. Little is therefore known about the Nervii perspective on the battle.

Bitka na reki Sabis, znana tudi (verjetno napačno) kot bitka na Sambri ali bitka proti Nervijem, je potekala leta 57 pr. n. št. blizu današnjega Saulzoirja na severu Francije. Ob reki Sabis se je rimska vojska pod poveljstvom Gaja Julija Cezarja spopadla z zvezo plemen Belgov, predvsem z Nerviji. Belgi so Cezarja z nenadnim napadom presenetili in ga skoraj premagali. Po Cezarjevih zapiskih so Rimljanom odločna obramba, spretno poveljevanje in pravočasen prihod okrepitev omogočili, da so zasedo Belgov spremenili v rimsko zmago. Malo primarnih virov bitko podrobno opisuje; večina podatkov izhaja iz Cezarjevega lastnega poročila v delu Zapiski o galski vojni (Commentarii de Bello Gallico). O tem, kako so bitko doživljali Nerviji, je zato malo znanega.

events.label: Battle of Morbihan
events.description: 56 BCE naval battle of the Gallic War

story.title: Battle of Morbihan
story.description: Rome v. Gallic Veneti, naval, Roman victory
paragraphs: The Battle of Morbihan, also known as the Battle of Quiberon Bay, was a naval battle fought in the summer of 56 BC between the Gallic tribe of the Veneti and a Roman fleet sent by Julius Caesar. The battle was fought off the coast of Brittany in modern-day France, likely near Quiberon Bay. The battle was a part of the Gallic Wars. The battle ended in a decisive Roman victory.

Bitka v Morbihanu, znana tudi kot bitka v zalivu Quiberon, je bila pomorska bitka poleti 56 pr. n. št. med galskim plemenom Venetov in rimsko floto, ki jo je poslal Julij Cezar. Potekala je pred obalo Bretanje v današnji Franciji, verjetno blizu zaliva Quiberon. Bila je del galskih vojn in se je končala z odločilno rimsko zmago.

events.label: Caesar's invasions of Britain
events.description: military campaigns in 55 and 54 BCE

story.title: Julius Caesar's invasions of Britain
story.description: Military campaigns in 55 and 54 BC
paragraphs: In the course of his Gallic Wars, Julius Caesar invaded Britain twice: in 55 and 54 BC. On the first occasion, Caesar took with him only two legions, and achieved little beyond a landing on the coast of Kent. The second invasion was more substantial, consisting of 800 ships, five legions and 2,000 cavalry. The Celtic Britons did not initially contest Caesar's landing, waiting instead until he began to move inland. Caesar eventually penetrated into Middlesex and crossed the Thames, forcing the British warlord Cassivellaunus to pay tribute to Rome and setting up Mandubracius of the Trinovantes as a client king. The Romans then returned to Gaul without conquering any territory.

Caesar included accounts of both invasions in his Commentarii de Bello Gallico, which contains the earliest surviving significant eyewitness descriptions of the island's people, culture and geography. This is effectively the start of the written history, or at least the protohistory, of Great Britain.

events.label: Ambiorix's Revolt
events.description: 53 BCE battle

story.title: Ambiorix's revolt
story.description: Belgae rebellion against Julius Caesar, winter 54 BCE – 53 BCE
paragraphs: Ambiorix's revolt was a rebellion of the Eburones tribe, triggered by the occupation of their territory by a part of Caesar's army. The uprising took place in the winter of 54–53 BCE and is part of Caesar's Gallic Wars. The tribe had appointed two war-leaders to command their warriors during their insurrection: Ambiorix and Catuvolcus. The revolt was afterwards named after Ambiorix, who played a more prominent role in the rebellion.

Discontent among the subjugated Gauls prompted a major uprising amongst the Belgae against Julius Caesar in the winter of 54–53 BCE, when the Eburones of north-eastern Gaul rose in rebellion. Fifteen Roman cohorts were wiped out at Atuatuca (modern Tongeren in Belgium) and a garrison commanded by Quintus Tullius Cicero narrowly survived after being relieved by Caesar in the nick of time. The rest of 53 BCE was occupied with a punitive campaign against the Eburones and their allies, who were said to have been all but exterminated by the Romans.

Ambioriksov upor je bil upor plemena Eburonov, ki so se uprli, ko je del Cezarjeve vojske zasedel njihovo ozemlje. Vstaja je potekala pozimi 54–53 pr. n. št. in je del Cezarjevih galskih vojn. Pleme je za poveljevanje bojevnikom med vstajo imenovalo dva vojna voditelja, Ambioriksa in Katuvolka. Upor je pozneje dobil ime po Ambioriksu, ki je imel v njem vidnejšo vlogo.

Nezadovoljstvo med podjarmljenimi Galci je pozimi 54–53 pr. n. št. sprožilo veliko vstajo Belgov proti Juliju Cezarju, ko so se uprli Eburoni na severovzhodu Galije. Pri Atuatuki (današnjem Tongerenu v Belgiji) je bilo uničenih petnajst rimskih kohort, posadka pod poveljstvom Kvinta Tulija Cicerona pa je komaj preživela, ker jo je Cezar v zadnjem trenutku osvobodil. Preostanek leta 53 pr. n. št. je minil v kazenskem pohodu proti Eburonom in njihovim zaveznikom, ki naj bi jih Rimljani skoraj iztrebili.

events.label: Battle of Carrhae
events.description: ancient battle between Roman Republic and Parthian Empire in 53 BCE near modern Harran, Turkey

story.title: Battle of Carrhae
story.description: Part of the Roman–Parthian Wars
paragraphs: The Battle of Carrhae (Latin pronunciation: [ˈkar.rʰae̯]) was fought in 53 BC between the Roman Republic and the Parthian Empire near the ancient town of Carrhae (present-day Harran, Turkey). An invading force of seven legions of Roman heavy infantry under Marcus Licinius Crassus was lured into the desert and decisively defeated by a mixed cavalry of armoured cataphracts and light horse archers led by the Parthian general Surena. On such flat terrain, the legion proved to have no viable tactics against the highly mobile Parthian horsemen, and the slow and vulnerable Roman formations were surrounded, exhausted by constant attacks, and eventually crushed. Crassus was killed along with most of his army. It is commonly seen as one of the earliest and most important battles between the Roman and Parthian Empires and one of the most crushing defeats in Roman history. According to the poet Ovid in Book 6 of his poem Fasti, the battle occurred on 9 June.

Crassus, a member of the First Triumvirate and the wealthiest man in Rome, had been enticed by the prospect of military glory and riches and decided to invade Parthia without the official consent of the Senate. Rejecting an offer from the Armenian King Artavasdes II to allow Crassus to invade Parthia via Armenia, Crassus marched his army directly through the deserts of Mesopotamia. His forces clashed with Surena's troops near Carrhae. Surena's cavalry killed or captured most of the Roman soldiers. Crassus was killed when truce negotiations turned violent, and his death ended the First Triumvirate.

events.label: Siege of Avaricum
events.description: battle of the Gallic Wars

events.label: Battle of Gergovia
events.description: victory of Gallic forces led by Vercingetorix over a Roman army led by Julius Caesar

story.title: Battle of Gergovia
story.description: Roman siege in 52 BC of stronghold of Vercingetorix's Gauls
paragraphs: The Battle of Gergovia took place in 52 BC in Gaul at Gergovia, the chief oppidum (fortified town) of the Arverni. The battle was fought between a Roman Republican army, led by proconsul Julius Caesar, and Gallic forces led by Vercingetorix, who was also the Arverni chieftain. The Romans attempted to besiege Gergovia, but miscommunication ruined the Roman plan. The Gallic cavalry counterattacked the confused Romans and sent them to flight, winning the battle.

The site is identified with Merdogne, since renamed Gergovie, a village located on a hill within the town of La Roche-Blanche, near Clermont-Ferrand, in south central France. Some walls and earthworks still survive from the pre-Roman Iron Age. The battle is well known in France as an example of a Gallic victory.

Bitka pri Gergoviji je potekala leta 52 pr. n. št. v Galiji pri Gergoviji, glavnem opidu (utrjenem mestu) Arvernov. V njej sta se spopadli vojska rimske republike pod vodstvom prokonzula Julija Cezarja in galske sile pod vodstvom Vercingetoriksa, ki je bil tudi arvernski poglavar. Rimljani so skušali Gergovijo oblegati, a so jim načrt pokvarili nesporazumi. Galska konjenica je zmedene Rimljane napadla, jih pognala v beg in dobila bitko.

Kraj enačijo z vasjo Merdogne, pozneje preimenovano v Gergovie, ki leži na griču v občini La Roche-Blanche blizu Clermont-Ferranda v južni osrednji Franciji. Ohranili so se nekateri zidovi in zemeljski okopi iz predrimske železne dobe. Bitka je v Franciji znana kot primer galske zmage.

events.label: Battle of Lutetia
events.description: 51 BCE battle

story.title: Battle of Lutetia
story.description: 52 BC battle between Roman and Gallic forces, part of Caesar's Gallic Wars
paragraphs: The Battle of Lutetia was fought in 52 BC on the plain of Grenelle in what is now Paris, between Roman forces under Titus Labienus and an anti-Roman Gallic coalition during the Gallic Wars. The Romans were victorious. Julius Caesar offers an account of the battle in his Gallic Wars, for which he draws both on Labienus' report and an episode in Polybius's history.

Bitka za Lutecijo je potekala leta 52 pr. n. št. na ravnini Grenelle na območju današnjega Pariza med rimskimi silami pod poveljstvom Tita Labiena in protirimsko galsko koalicijo v galskih vojnah. Zmagali so Rimljani. Julij Cezar bitko opisuje v svojih Zapiskih o galski vojni, pri čemer se opira tako na Labienovo poročilo kot na epizodo iz Polibijeve zgodovine.

events.label: Battle of Alesia
events.description: decisive Roman victory in which Rome secures the conquest of Gaul

story.title: Battle of Alesia
story.description: Part of the Gallic Wars
paragraphs: The Battle of Alesia or Siege of Alesia (September 52 BC) was the climactic military engagement of the Gallic Wars, fought around the Gallic oppidum (fortified settlement) of Alesia in modern France, a major centre of the Mandubii tribe. It was fought by the Roman army of Julius Caesar against a confederation of Gallic tribes united under the leadership of Vercingetorix of the Arverni. It was the last major engagement between Gauls and Romans, and is considered one of Caesar's greatest military achievements and a classic example of siege warfare and investment; the Roman army built dual lines of fortifications—an inner wall to keep the besieged Gauls in, and an outer wall to keep the Gallic relief force out. The Battle of Alesia marked the end of Gallic independence in the modern day territory of France and Belgium.
Archeological and historical research confirms that the battle site was most probably atop Mont Auxois, above modern Alise-Sainte-Reine in France.

The event is described by Caesar himself in his Commentarii de Bello Gallico as well as several later ancient authors (namely Plutarch and Cassius Dio). After the Roman victory, Gaul (very roughly modern France) was subdued, although Gallic territories north of Gallia Narbonensis would not become a Roman province until 27 BCE. The Roman Senate granted Caesar a thanksgiving of 20 days for his victory in the Gallic War.

events.label: crossing the Rubicon
events.description: historical event and idiom

story.title: Crossing the Rubicon
story.description: Idiom meaning a point of no return
paragraphs: The phrase "crossing the Rubicon" is an idiom meaning "passing the point of no return". Its meaning comes from the crossing of the Rubicon river by Julius Caesar in January 49 BC at the head of the 13th Legion. Caesar was not allowed to command an army within Italy proper, and by crossing the river with his forces was defying law and risking death. The crossing precipitated a civil war, which eventually led to Caesar becoming dictator for life (dictator perpetuo).

Caesar had previously been appointed governor of a region that stretched from southern Gaul to Illyricum. As his term was coming to an end, the Senate ordered him to disband his army and return to Rome. Caesar defied the order, and instead brought his army to Rome, occupying the city of Ariminum then crossing the Rubicon towards the south. The exact date of the crossing is unknown, but scholars usually place it on the night of 10 and 11 January because of the speeds at which messengers could travel at that time. The phrase alea iacta est ("the die is cast"), allegedly uttered by Caesar just before the crossing, also comes from this event.

Besedna zveza »prečkanje Rubikona« je idiom, ki pomeni »prestopiti točko, od koder ni vrnitve«. Izvira iz prečkanja reke Rubikon, ki ga je Julij Cezar januarja 49 pr. n. št. opravil na čelu 13. legije. Cezarju ni bilo dovoljeno poveljevati vojski znotraj same Italije, zato je s prečkanjem reke s svojimi četami kršil zakon in tvegal smrt. Prečkanje je sprožilo državljansko vojno, zaradi katere je Cezar nazadnje postal dosmrtni diktator (dictator perpetuo).

editorial.why: The act that began Caesar's Civil War; Wikidata links it to no war.
editorial.quote: crossing of the Rubicon river by Julius Caesar in January 49 BC

events.label: Siege of Massilia
events.description: 49 BCE military blockade and naval battle, part of Caesar's civil war against Pompey

story.title: Siege of Massilia
story.description: 49 BC siege by forces loyal to Caesar
paragraphs: The siege of Massilia, including two naval engagements, was an episode of Caesar's Civil War, fought in 49 BC between forces loyal to the Optimates and a detachment of Caesar's army. The siege was conducted by Gaius Trebonius, one of Caesar's senior legates, while the naval operations were in the capable hands of Decimus Brutus, Caesar's naval expert.

Obleganje Massilie, ki je vključevalo tudi dva pomorska spopada, je bilo epizoda Cezarjeve državljanske vojne, ki je potekala leta 49 pr. n. št. med silami, zvestimi optimatom, in odredom Cezarjeve vojske. Obleganje je vodil Gaj Trebonij, eden Cezarjevih višjih legatov, pomorske operacije pa so bile v sposobnih rokah Decima Bruta, Cezarjevega strokovnjaka za pomorstvo.

events.label: Battle of Ilerda
events.description: battle between the forces of Julius Caesar and the Spanish army of Pompey the Great

story.title: Battle of Ilerda
story.description: 49 BC battle in modern-day Catalonia
paragraphs: The Battle of Ilerda took place in June 49 BC between the forces of Julius Caesar and the Hispanian army of Pompey Magnus, led by his legates Lucius Afranius and Marcus Petreius. Unlike many of the other battles of the civil war, this was more a campaign of manoeuvre than actual fighting. It allowed Caesar to eliminate the threat of Pompey's forces in Hispania and face Pompey himself in Greece at the Battle of Pharsalus (48 BC).

Bitka pri Ilerdi je potekala junija 49 pr. n. št. med silami Julija Cezarja in hispansko vojsko Pompeja Velikega, ki sta jo vodila njegova legata Lucij Afranij in Mark Petrej. V nasprotju s številnimi drugimi bitkami državljanske vojne je šlo bolj za manevrski pohod kot za prave boje. Cezarju je omogočil, da je odpravil nevarnost Pompejevih sil v Hispaniji in se s samim Pompejem spopadel v Grčiji v bitki pri Farzalu (48 pr. n. št.).

events.label: Battle of the Bagradas River
events.description: between Julius Caesar's general Gaius Scribonius Curio and the Pompeian Republicans under Publius Attius Varus and King Juba I of Numidia

story.title: Battle of the Bagradas (49 BC)
story.description: North African battle of Caesar's civil war
paragraphs: The Battle of the Bagradas (49 BC) occurred near the Bagradas River (the classical name of the Medjerda) in what is now Tunisia on 24 August and was fought between Julius Caesar's general Gaius Scribonius Curio and the Pompeian Republicans under Publius Attius Varus and King Juba I of Numidia. The result was a crushing defeat for the Caesarean forces and the death of Curio.

Bitka pri Bagradi (49 pr. n. št.) je potekala 24. avgusta blizu reke Bagrade (antično ime reke Medžerde) na ozemlju današnje Tunizije med Cezarjevim vojskovodjo Gajem Skribonijem Kurionom ter pompejanskimi republikanci pod Publijem Atijem Varom in numidijskim kraljem Jubo I. Končala se je s hudim porazom Cezarjevih sil in Kurionovo smrtjo.

events.label: Battle of Dyrrhachium
events.description: battle of Caesar's Civil War in the area of the city of Dyrrachium (in what is now Albania)

story.title: Battle of Dyrrhachium (48 BC)
story.description: Siege battle, part of Caesar's civil war
paragraphs: The Battle of Dyrrachium (or Dyrrhachium) took place from April to late July 48 BC near the city of Dyrrachium (modern-day Durrës) in what is now Albania. It was fought between Gaius Julius Caesar and an army led by Gnaeus Pompey during Caesar's civil war.

Caesar attempted to capture the vital Pompeian logistics hub of Dyrrachium, but was unsuccessful after Pompey occupied it and the surrounding heights. In response, Caesar besieged Pompey's camp and constructed a circumvallation thereof, until after months of skirmishes, Pompey was able to break through Caesar's fortified lines, forcing Caesar to make a strategic retreat into Thessaly.
After the battle, Pompey pursued Caesar into Thessaly and then towards Pharsalus, where the decisive battle of Caesar's Greek campaign would be fought.

Bitka pri Dirahiju je potekala od aprila do konca julija 48 pr. n. št. blizu mesta Dirahij (današnji Drač) na ozemlju današnje Albanije. V njej sta se v Cezarjevi državljanski vojni spopadla Gaj Julij Cezar in vojska pod vodstvom Gneja Pompeja.

Cezar je skušal zavzeti Dirahij, ključno oskrbovalno središče Pompejancev, vendar mu ni uspelo, ker je Pompej zasedel mesto in okoliške vzpetine.
